title.zh: 卷二百八十五 列傳第四十四 陳執中 劉沆 馮拯 賈昌朝 梁適
title.en: Volume 285 Biographies 44: Chen Zhizhong, Liu Hang, Feng Zheng, Jia Changchao, Liang Shi
title.raw: 卷二百八十五 列傳第四十四 陳執中 劉沆 馮拯 賈昌朝 梁適 Volume 285 Biographies 44: Chen Zhizhong, Liu Hang, Feng Zheng, Jia Changchao, Liang Shi

sentences.zh: 陳執中

translations.literal: Chen Zhizhong
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhizhong

sentences.zh: 陳執中，字昭譽，以父恕任，為秘書省正字，累遷衛尉寺丞、知梧州。

translations.literal: Chen Zhizhong, styled Zhaoyu, entered office through his father's privilege of appointment, became a proofreader in the Secretariat, and was promoted in succession to Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Stud and Prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhizhong, courtesy name Zhaoyu, received his first appointment through his father's yin privilege and served as proofreader in the Secretariat. He rose in turn to vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Stud and prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上《復古要道》三篇，真宗異而召之。

translations.literal: He submitted three essays entitled "Essentials for Restoring Antiquity," and Emperor Zhenzong, impressed, summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He presented three memorials on "Essentials for Returning to Antiquity," and Zhenzong, struck by them, called him to court.

sentences.zh: 帝屬疾，春秋高，大臣莫敢言建儲者，執中進《演要》三篇，以蚤定天下根本為說。

translations.literal: The emperor was ill and advanced in years; none among the great ministers dared speak of establishing an heir. Zhizhong presented three essays entitled "Expository Essentials," arguing that the root of the realm should be settled early.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was ailing and well advanced in years, and none of the chief ministers dared broach the question of naming an heir. Zhizhong submitted three essays entitled Expository Essentials, urging that the foundations of the empire be secured without delay.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝以他疏示輔臣，皆讚曰 “善”。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor showed the chief ministers another memorial, and all praised it, saying "Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: The following day the emperor showed his senior advisers another memorial, and they all exclaimed that it was excellent.

sentences.zh: 帝指其袖中曰：“又有善於此者。”

translations.literal: The emperor pointed to his sleeve and said, "There is something even better than this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tapped his sleeve and said, "I have something still better than that."

sentences.zh: 出之，乃《演要》也。

translations.literal: He brought it out, and it was the Expository Essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He produced it—the Expository Essentials.

sentences.zh: 因召對便殿，勞問久之，擢右正言。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was summoned for audience in the side hall, questioned and commended at length, and promoted to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was then summoned to the side hall for a lengthy audience and commendation, and promoted to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 逾月，遂立皇太子。

translations.literal: More than a month later, the crown prince was duly installed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the heir apparent had been formally named.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐考禦試進士卷差謬，貶衛尉寺丞、監岳州酒務。

translations.literal: The next year, because of errors in grading the palace examination papers of jinshi candidates, he was demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Stud and superintendent of the wine monopoly in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was demoted for mistakes in grading the palace examination papers, reduced to vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Stud and put in charge of the Yuezhou wine tax.

sentences.zh: 稍復殿中丞、通判撫州，復右正言。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to Palace Aide, made supervisory prefect of Fuzhou, and again received the post of Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as palace aide and supervisory prefect of Fuzhou, and again made Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 曹利用婿盧士倫除福建運使，憚遠不行，利用為請，乃改京東。

translations.literal: Lu Shilun, son-in-law of Cao Utilize, was appointed transport commissioner for Fujian but feared the distance and would not go. Utilize pleaded on his behalf, and the appointment was changed to Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Utilize's son-in-law Lu Shilun was appointed Fujian transport commissioner but shrank from the distant posting; Utilize intervened and the post was switched to the Eastern Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 執中嘗劾奏之，利用挾私忿，出執中知漢陽軍。

translations.literal: Zhizhong had once impeached him; Utilize, nursing a private grudge, had Zhizhong sent out as military prefect of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong had previously impeached him; Utilize, bearing a private grudge, had Zhizhong posted out as military prefect of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 及利用得罪，乃召為群牧判官、權三司鹽鐵判官、知諫院、提舉諸司庫務，以尚書工部員外郎兼御史知雜、同判流內銓，遷三司戶部副使。

translations.literal: When Utilize fell from grace, Zhizhong was recalled as aide in the Pasturage Commission, acting Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments, head of the Remonstrance Bureau, and commissioner overseeing the treasuries of various offices; as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat with concurrent duty as miscellaneous censor and associate director of the Inner Stream Bureau, he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Revenue Section of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: After Utilize's disgrace Zhizhong was recalled to a string of central posts: aide in the Pasturage Commission, acting salt and iron commissioner, head of the Remonstrance Bureau, and overseer of government storehouses. As vice director of works with concurrent censorial and personnel duties, he rose to vice commissioner of the Three Departments' revenue section.

sentences.zh: 明道中，安撫京東，進天章閣待制。

translations.literal: During the Mingdao reign period he pacified Jingdong and was advanced to Hanlin academician awaiting appointment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Mingdao era he served as pacification commissioner for Jingdong and was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation.

sentences.zh: 使還，知應天府，徙江寧府、揚州，再遷工部郎中，改龍圖閣直學士、知永興軍，拜右諫議大夫、同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission he was made prefect of Yingtianfu, then transferred to Jiangningfu and Yangzhou; promoted again to Director of the Ministry of Works, then made Dragon Diagram Hall academician and military prefect of Yongxing; appointed Right Censor-in-Chief and Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from his assignment he governed Yingtianfu, then Jiangning and Yangzhou. He was promoted to director of works, made Dragon Diagram Hall academician and military prefect of Yongxing, and appointed right censor-in-chief and associate commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇延州，手詔諮訪輔臣攻守方略，執中既上對，退，復奏疏曰：“元昊乘中國久不用兵，竊發西垂，以遊兵困勁卒、甘言悅守臣，一旦連犯亭障，延安幾至不保。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao raided Yanzhou, the emperor by autograph edict consulted the chief ministers on offensive and defensive strategy. After Zhizhong had answered at audience, he withdrew and submitted a further memorial, saying: "Yuan Hao, taking advantage of China's long disuse of arms, secretly rose in the western marches, using roaming troops to wear down crack soldiers and sweet words to please frontier commanders. In a single stroke he successively violated the border posts, and Yan'an nearly could not be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao attacked Yanzhou, the emperor issued a handwritten edict asking his senior ministers for plans of attack and defense. Zhizhong answered at court, then on retiring submitted a further memorial: "Yuan Hao, exploiting the fact that the empire had long gone without war, secretly struck in the western marches. He used skirmishing forces to exhaust our best troops and blandishments to win over frontier commanders. In one swift campaign he overran a chain of border posts, and Yan'an nearly fell."

sentences.zh: 此蓋范雍納詭說，失於戒嚴；

translations.literal: This was because Fan Yong accepted deceptive counsel and failed in vigilance;
translations.idiomatic: This was because Fan Yong had accepted deceptive advice and let his guard down;

sentences.zh: 劉平輕躁，喪其所部。

translations.literal: Liu Ping was rash and lost his command.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping acted rashly and lost his entire force.

sentences.zh: 上下紛攘，遠近震駭。

translations.literal: Court and country were thrown into turmoil, and near and far were shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The court and the realm were thrown into turmoil, and alarm spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 自金明李士彬族破，而並邊籬落皆大壞。

translations.literal: Since the clan of Li Shibin of Jinming was destroyed, the frontier stockades along the border were greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the destruction of Li Shibin's clan at Jinming, the frontier stockades along the border had been largely wrecked.

sentences.zh: 塞門、金明相距二百里，宜列修三城，城屯兵千人，益募弓箭手。

translations.literal: Saimen and Jinming are two hundred li apart; three cities should be built in a line, each garrisoned with a thousand troops, and archers should be recruited in addition.
translations.idiomatic: Saimen and Jinming lie two hundred li apart; three fortified towns should be built in a line, each holding a thousand troops, with additional archers recruited.

sentences.zh: 寇大至則退保，小至則出鬥。

translations.literal: When the enemy comes in force they should withdraw to the fortifications; when they come in small bands they should sally out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy came in strength they would fall back to the forts; when raiders came in small bands they would sally out to fight.

sentences.zh: 選閣門祗候以上為寨主、都監，以諸司使為盧關一路都巡檢，以兵二千屬之，使為三砦之援。

translations.literal: Men of Gate Attendant rank and above should be chosen as stockade chiefs and chief supervisors; a commissioner of various offices should be made overall inspector of the Luguan route, with two thousand troops placed under him to serve as reinforcement for the three stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Gate attendants and higher officers should be appointed stockade chiefs and chief supervisors; a bureau commissioner should serve as overall inspector of the Luguan route with two thousand troops under him to reinforce the three stockades.

sentences.zh: 熟羌居漢地久者，委邊臣拊存之；

translations.literal: Acculturated Qiang who have long lived under Han rule should be entrusted to frontier officials to comfort and preserve;
translations.idiomatic: Acculturated Qiang who had long lived under Han rule should be left to frontier officials to reassure and support;

sentences.zh: 反覆者，破逐之。

translations.literal: those who waver should be broken and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: those who wavered should be crushed and expelled.

sentences.zh: 至於新拊黠羌，如涇原康奴、滅臧、大蟲族，久居內地，常有叛心，不肆剪除，恐終為患。

translations.literal: As for newly pacified crafty Qiang such as the Kangnu, Miezang, and Dachong tribes of Jingyuan, who have long dwelt in the interior and often harbor rebellious intent—if they are not thoroughly cut down, I fear they will ultimately become a menace.
translations.idiomatic: As for newly pacified but treacherous Qiang such as the Kangnu, Miezang, and Dachong clans of Jingyuan, who had long lived in the interior and often harbored rebellious designs—unless they were rooted out, they would surely become a lasting threat.

sentences.zh: 今軍須之出，民已愁歎，復欲遍修城池如河北之制，及夏須成，使神運之猶恐不能，民力其堪此乎？

translations.literal: Now military supplies are being levied and the people already groan with distress; yet there is a further wish to repair city walls everywhere on the Hebei model. Even if divine transport were employed, I fear it could not be finished by summer—and can the people's strength bear this?
translations.idiomatic: Military levies already had the people groaning in distress, yet some wished to rebuild city walls everywhere on the Hebei model. Even with supernatural logistics it might not be finished by summer—how could the people's strength bear such a burden?

sentences.zh: 陝西地險，非如河北，惟涇州、鎮戎軍勢稍平易，若不責外守而勞內營，非策之上也。

translations.literal: Shaanxi's terrain is perilous, unlike Hebei; only Jingzhou and Zhenrong Army have somewhat level ground. If one does not charge the outer garrisons with defense but instead exhausts the interior with construction, this is not the best policy.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi's terrain was rugged, unlike Hebei; only Jingzhou and Zhenrong Army offered somewhat level ground. To burden the interior with construction rather than holding the outer line was poor strategy.

sentences.zh: 宜修並邊城池，其次如延州之鄜、同，環慶之邠、寧，不過五七處，量為營葺，則科率減、民力蘇矣。

translations.literal: It is fitting to repair the border cities along the frontier; next, places such as Fu and Tong under Yanzhou, and Bin and Ning under Huanqing—no more than five or seven sites—should be built up as needed, so that levies would be reduced and the people's strength would recover.
translations.idiomatic: The border cities along the frontier should be repaired; next, only five or seven places such as Fu and Tong under Yanzhou and Bin and Ning under Huanqing need be fortified as required, so levies would fall and the people could recover.

sentences.zh: 今賊勢方張，宜靜守以驕其志，蓄銳以挫其鋒，增土兵以備守禦，省騎卒以減轉餉。

translations.literal: Now the enemy's power is on the rise; it is fitting to hold quietly to make them arrogant, store sharp troops to blunt their edge, increase local militia for defense, and reduce cavalry to cut transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy's power still rising, we should hold our positions quietly to lull their arrogance, husband our strength to blunt their momentum, increase local militia for defense, and cut cavalry to reduce supply transport.

sentences.zh: 然後徐議蕩平，改張節度，更須主張，將臣橫議不入，則忠臣盡節而捐軀矣。”

translations.literal: Only then should one slowly discuss pacification, change and expand the military commissions, and have a firm hand at the top. If generals and ministers thrust in reckless counsel unheeded, then loyal subjects will exhaust their devotion and give their lives in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could we slowly plan a full pacification, reorganize the military commissions, and keep a firm hand at the top. Unless reckless counsel from generals and ministers was kept out, loyal men would exhaust themselves and die for nothing.

sentences.zh: 既而議刺土兵，久不決，罷知青州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, deliberation on branding local militia dragged on without resolution, and he was dismissed from his post as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Debate over branding local militia then dragged on without resolution, and he was removed as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以資政殿學士知河南府，改尚書工部侍郎、陝西同經略安撫招討使。

translations.literal: He was again made Zizheng Hall academician and prefect of Henanfu, then changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and co-commissioner for pacification, comfort, and punitive campaigns in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Zizheng Hall academician and prefect of Henan, then promoted to vice director of works and co-commissioner for pacification and punitive campaigns in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 與夏竦同知永興軍，議邊事多異同，詔令互出巡邊，乃屯涇州，令諸部曰：“寇籍吾水草，鈔邊圖利，不除，且復至。”

translations.literal: Together with Xia Song he served as co-military prefect of Yongxing; they often differed on frontier affairs, and an edict ordered them to tour the border in turn. He then encamped at Jingzhou and ordered the various departments: "The enemy rely on our pasture and water, raid the border for profit—if they are not eliminated, they will come again."
translations.idiomatic: Serving with Xia Song as co-military prefect of Yongxing, he often clashed with him over frontier policy, and the court ordered them to inspect the border in turn. He encamped at Jingzhou and told the departments: "The enemy depend on our pasture and water and raid the border for profit—unless we destroy them, they will return."

sentences.zh: 命悉焚之。

translations.literal: He ordered all of it burned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered everything burned.

sentences.zh: 表解兵柄，以為兵尚神密，千里稟命，非所以制勝，宜屬四路各保疆圉。

translations.literal: He memorialized to relinquish military authority, arguing that warfare values secrecy, and that receiving orders from a thousand li away is not how to win; each of the four circuits should be charged with guarding its own territory.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to surrender military authority, arguing that war demands secrecy and that taking orders from a thousand li away cannot win battles; each of the four frontier circuits should defend its own territory.

sentences.zh: 朝議善之，就知陝州，復徙青州。

translations.literal: The court approved this view and appointed him prefect of Shaanzhou, then transferred him again to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal and made him prefect of Shaanzhou, then transferred him again to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是請城傅海諸州，朝廷重興役，有詔不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested fortification of the Fu Sea prefectures; the court, wary of renewed corvée labor, issued an edict forbidding it.
translations.idiomatic: He then sought to fortify the coastal Fu Sea prefectures, but the court, reluctant to impose new corvée labor, issued an edict forbidding it.

sentences.zh: 執中不奉詔，卒城之。

translations.literal: Zhizhong did not obey the edict and in the end built the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong defied the edict and completed the fortifications anyway.

sentences.zh: 明年，沂卒王倫叛，趣淮南，執中遣巡檢傅永吉追至采石磯，捕殺之。

translations.literal: The next year the Yi garrison soldier Wang Lun rebelled and hastened toward Huainan. Zhizhong sent the inspector Fu Yongji in pursuit to Caishiji, where he captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the garrison soldier Wang Lun of Yi rebelled and marched toward Huainan. Zhizhong sent inspector Fu Yongji in pursuit to Caishiji, where Wang was captured and killed.

sentences.zh: 召拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 諫官孫甫、蔡襄極論不可，帝遣使馳賜敕告。

translations.literal: The remonstrating officials Sun Fu and Cai Xiang argued strenuously that this should not be done; the emperor sent a courier bearing an edict of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators Sun Fu and Cai Xiang argued fiercely against the appointment, but the emperor sent a courier with an edict confirming it.

sentences.zh: 逾年，拜同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士兼樞密使。

translations.literal: More than a year later he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Tongzhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi rank, Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made grand councilor, grand academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and concurrent commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 西夏納款，與宰相賈昌朝請解樞密。

translations.literal: When Western Xia submitted tribute, he and the chief minister Jia Changchao requested to be relieved of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Xia submitted, he and chief minister Jia Changchao asked to be relieved of their military affairs posts.

sentences.zh: 七年春，旱，昌朝罷，執中降給事中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year there was drought; Changchao was dismissed, and Zhizhong was demoted to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year a drought struck; Changchao was dismissed and Zhizhong was demoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 已而加昭文館大學士、監修國史，逾月復官。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional titles of Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and supervisor of the compilation of the national history; more than a month later his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall and supervisor of the national history; within a month his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，以足疾辭位，自陳不願為使相、大學士，學士孫抃當制，遂以尚書左丞知陳州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huangyou reign he resigned his post because of foot ailment, stating that he did not wish to be a commissioner-delegate or grand academician. Academician Sun Bian drafted the appointment, and he was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huangyou era he resigned because of a foot ailment, declaring that he did not wish to remain a commissioner-delegate or grand academician. When academician Sun Bian drafted the edict, Zhizhong was made left vice director of the secretariat and prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宰相文彥博、宋庠以為禮薄，帖麻改兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The chief ministers Wen Yanbo and Song Qi considered the honors too slight; an edict on hemp paper was posted changing his title to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Wen Yanbo and Song Qi thought the appointment too modest; an edict was issued promoting him to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部、觀文殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and made Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the ministry of personnel and made grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜集慶軍節度使、同平章事、判大名府。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was appointed military commissioner of Jiqing Army, Associate Grand Councilor, and administrator of Damingfu.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed military commissioner of Jiqing Army, associate grand councilor, and administrator of Daming.

sentences.zh: 河決商胡，走大名，程琳欲為堤，不果成而去。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks at Shanghu and flowed toward Daming. Cheng Lin wished to build a dike but could not complete it and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River broke through at Shanghu and surged toward Daming. Cheng Lin tried to build a dike but could not finish it before he left office.

sentences.zh: 執中乘年豐調丁夫增築二十里，以障橫潰。

translations.literal: Zhizhong, taking advantage of a bountiful year, levied corvée laborers to extend the dike twenty li to block the breach.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong took advantage of a good harvest year to levy laborers and extend the dike twenty li to contain the breach.

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書復拜同平章事、昭文館大學士。

translations.literal: As Minister of Personnel he was again appointed Associate Grand Councilor and Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of personnel he was again appointed associate grand councilor and grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 每朝退，閉中書東便門，以防漏泄。

translations.literal: After each court session he closed the east side gate of the Secretariat to prevent leaks.
translations.idiomatic: After each court session he shut the east side gate of the Secretariat to prevent leaks.

sentences.zh: 三司勾當公事及監場務官，權勢所引者，皆奏罷之，內外為之肅然。

translations.literal: Officials handling Three Departments business and supervisors of market posts who had been advanced through powerful connections were all memorialized for dismissal, and within and without the court were awed into order because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Officials handling Three Departments business and market supervisors who had been advanced through powerful patrons were all memorialized for dismissal, and the court and the realm were awed into order.

sentences.zh: 執中在中書八年，人莫敢幹以私，四方問遺不及門，惟殿前都指揮使郭承祐數至其家，為御史所言，遂詔中書、樞密自今非聚廳無見賓客。

translations.literal: Zhizhong was in the Secretariat for eight years; no one dared approach him with private requests, and gifts from the four quarters did not reach his door—only the Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front Guard Guo Chengyou came to his house repeatedly. When the censors spoke of this, an edict was issued that henceforth the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs were not to receive guests except in full assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong spent eight years in the Secretariat; no one dared approach him with private requests, and gifts from across the realm never reached his door—only palace front guard commander Guo Chenyou visited repeatedly. When the censors reported this, an edict ordered that the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs receive no guests except in full assembly.

sentences.zh: 及議諡，禮官韓維曰：“執中以公卿子，遭世承平，因緣一言，遂至貴顯。

translations.literal: When his posthumous title was debated, the ritual official Han Wei said: "Zhizhong, as the son of a high minister, encountered a peaceful age and, through a single remark, rose to eminent rank."
translations.idiomatic: When his posthumous title was debated, ritual official Han Wei said: "Zhizhong, born the son of a high minister in a peaceful age, rose to eminence on the strength of a single remark."

sentences.zh: 天子以後宮之喪，問所以葬祭之禮，執中位上相，不能總率群司考正儀典，知治喪皇儀非嬪禦之禮，追冊位號於宮闈有嫌，建廟用樂逾祖宗舊制，皆白而行之，此不忠之大者。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven, on the death of a woman of the inner palace, asked about rites of burial and sacrifice, Zhizhong, holding the rank of chief minister, could not lead the various offices in examining and correcting the ritual codes. He knew that imperial funeral rites were not the rites for a consort, that posthumous enfeoffment in the inner quarters was improper, and that building a temple and using music beyond the ancestral regulations were wrong—yet he reported these things and carried them out. This was a grave failure of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor, mourning a woman of the inner palace, asked about burial and sacrifice, Zhizhong as chief minister failed to lead the ministries in correcting the ritual codes. He knew that imperial funeral rites were not those for a consort, that posthumous titles from the inner quarters were improper, and that building a temple with music beyond ancestral precedent was wrong—yet he reported these measures and carried them out. This was gross disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 閨門之內，禮分不明，夫人正室疏薄自絀，庶妾賤人悍逸不制，其治家無足言者。

translations.literal: Within the women's quarters ritual distinctions were unclear: the lawful wife was neglected and humbled herself, while low concubines were fierce and unrestrained. His management of the household is not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Within his household ritual order broke down: his lawful wife was neglected and demeaned herself, while low concubines were fierce and unrestrained. His domestic governance was beneath comment.

sentences.zh: 宰相不能秉道率禮，正身齊家，方杜門深居，謝絕賓客，曰：‘我無私也，我不黨也。

translations.literal: A chief minister who could not uphold the Way and lead in ritual, who could not rectify himself and order his household, instead shut his doors and lived in seclusion, refusing guests, saying, 'I have no private interests; I form no factions.'
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister who could not uphold the Way, lead in ritual, or order his own household instead shut his doors, lived in seclusion, and refused guests, saying, 'I have no private interests; I form no factions.'

sentences.zh: ’豈不陋哉？

translations.literal: ' Is this not shabby?
translations.idiomatic: ' Is that not contemptible?

sentences.zh: 諡法：‘寵祿光大曰榮’，‘不勤成名曰靈’。

translations.literal: The posthumous-title canon says: 'Glory' is for one whose favor and emoluments shine greatly; 'Spirit' is for one who achieves a name without diligence.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous-title canon says: 'Glory' applies when favor and emoluments shine greatly; 'Spirit' applies when one gains a name without diligence.

sentences.zh: 執中出入將相，以一品就第，寵祿光大矣；

translations.literal: Zhizhong moved between general and minister, retired to his estate with the first rank—his favor and emoluments shone greatly;
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong rose through general and minister to retire with the first rank—his favor and emoluments had indeed shone greatly;

sentences.zh: 得位行政，賢士大夫無述焉，不勤成名矣；

translations.literal: he gained office and administered affairs, yet worthy gentlemen and great officers have nothing to recount of him—he achieved a name without diligence;
translations.idiomatic: he held office and governed, yet worthy gentlemen have nothing to recount of him—he had gained a name without diligence;

sentences.zh: 請諡曰榮靈。”

translations.literal: I request the posthumous title Rongling [Glory-Spirit]."
translations.idiomatic: I propose the posthumous title Glory-Spirit."

sentences.zh: 後改諡恭襄，詔諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Later it was changed to Gongxiang [Respectful-Aid], and an edict gave the posthumous title Gong [Respectful].
translations.idiomatic: It was later changed to Respectful-Aid, and an edict finally granted the posthumous title Respectful.

sentences.zh: 帝篆其墓碑曰“褒忠之碑”。

translations.literal: The emperor inscribed his tomb stele "Stele in Praise of Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inscribed his tomb stele "Stele in Praise of Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 子世儒，官至國子博士，妻李與群婢殺世儒所生母，世儒與謀，皆棄市。

translations.literal: His son Shiru rose to Erudite of the Imperial University. Shiru's wife Li, together with a group of maidservants, killed Shiru's birth mother; Shiru joined in the plot, and all were executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiru rose to erudite of the Imperial University. Shiru's wife Li and several maidservants murdered his birth mother with Shiru's complicity, and all were executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 劉沆，字冲之，吉州永新人。

translations.literal: Liu Hang, styled Chongzhi, was a native of Yongxin in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hang, courtesy name Chongzhi, was a native of Yongxin in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖景洪，始，楊行密得江西，衙將彭玕據州自稱太守，屬景洪以兵，欲脅眾附湖南，景洪偽許之。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing Hong: at the beginning, when Yang Xingmi took Jiangxi, the yamen guard Peng Gan seized the prefecture and styled himself prefect, assigning troops to Jing Hong and wishing to coerce the multitude into submitting to Hunan. Jing Hong falsely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing Hong: when Yang Xingmi seized Jiangxi, yamen guard Peng Gan took the prefecture and styled himself prefect. He assigned troops to Jing Hong and tried to coerce the people into submitting to Hunan; Jing Hong pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 復以州歸行密，退居不仕。

translations.literal: He then returned the prefecture to Xingmi and withdrew to live in retirement without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned the prefecture to Xingmi and retired without taking office.

sentences.zh: 及徐溫建國，以禮聘之，不起，官其子煦為殿直都虞候。

translations.literal: When Xu Wen founded his state, he invited Jing Hong with full ceremony, but Jing Hong did not rise to serve; Wen enfeoffed his son Xu as Palace Attendant and Chief Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Wen founded his state he invited Jing Hong with full ceremony, but Jing Hong refused to serve; Wen instead appointed his son Xu as palace attendant and chief commandant.

sentences.zh: 父素，不仕，以財雄里中，喜賓客。

translations.literal: His father Su did not take office; by wealth he dominated the neighborhood and delighted in entertaining guests.
translations.idiomatic: His father Su never held office but dominated the neighborhood through wealth and delighted in entertaining guests.

sentences.zh: 景洪嘗告人曰：“我不從彭玕，幾活萬人，後世當有隆者。”

translations.literal: Jing Hong once told others: "Had I not refused Peng Gan, I would nearly have kept ten thousand people alive; posterity will surely produce one who rises high."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hong once said: "By refusing Peng Gan I nearly saved ten thousand lives; our descendants will surely produce someone who rises high."

sentences.zh: 因名所居北山曰後隆山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he named the northern mountain where he dwelt Mount Later Prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore named the northern mountain where he lived Mount Later Prosperity.

sentences.zh: 山有牛僧孺讀書堂，即故基築台曰聰明台。

translations.literal: On the mountain was Niú Sēng'rú's study hall; on that old foundation he built a terrace called the Terrace of Cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: On the mountain stood Niú Sēng'rú's study hall; on its old foundations he built a terrace called the Terrace of Cleverness.

sentences.zh: 沆母夢衣冠丈夫曰牛相公來，已來有娠，乃生沆。

translations.literal: Hang's mother dreamed of a man in cap and robes who said, "Minister Niu has come." After he came she was with child, and thus Hang was born.
translations.idiomatic: Hang's mother dreamed of a man in official dress who said, "Minister Niu has arrived." After the dream she conceived, and Hang was born.

sentences.zh: 及長，倜儻任氣。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was free-spirited and bold.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was free-spirited and headstrong.

sentences.zh: 舉進士不中，自稱“退士”，不復出，父力勉之。

translations.literal: He took the jinshi examination but did not pass, styled himself "the retired scholar," and would not go out again; his father urged him strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination, styled himself "the retired scholar," and refused to try again until his father pressed him hard.

sentences.zh: 天聖八年，始擢進士第二，為大理評事、通判舒州，有大獄曆歲不決，沆數日決之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiansheng he was at last placed second among jinshi graduates, appointed Reviewing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review and supervisory prefect of Shuzhou. A major case had gone unresolved for a year; Hang settled it in a few days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tiansheng he finally placed second among jinshi graduates and was made reviewing clerk of the Court of Judicial Review and supervisory prefect of Shuzhou. A major case had dragged on for a year; Hang resolved it in a few days.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后建資聖浮圖，內侍張懷信挾詔命，督役嚴峻，州將至移疾不敢出，沆奏罷懷信。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhangxian was building the Zisheng pagoda; the inner attendant Zhang Huaixin, bearing an edict, supervised the labor with harsh severity. The prefect was about to plead illness and dared not go out; Hang memorialized to dismiss Huaixin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhangxian was building the Zisheng pagoda; eunuch Zhang Huaixin, wielding an edict, supervised the work with brutal severity until the prefect nearly feigned illness rather than face him. Hang memorialized to have Huaixin removed.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常丞、直集賢院，出知衡州。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and entered the Hall for Gathering Worthies as academician, then sent out as prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, then posted as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 大姓尹氏欺鄰翁老子幼，欲竊取其田，乃偽作賣券，及鄰翁死，遂奪而有之。

translations.literal: The great clan Yin, taking advantage of an elderly neighbor whose son was young, wished to seize his fields. They forged a deed of sale, and when the neighbor died they seized and held the land.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful Yin clan, seeing that an elderly neighbor had only a young son, forged a deed of sale and seized his fields after the old man died.

sentences.zh: 其子訴於州縣，二十年不得直，沆至，復訴之。

translations.literal: The son appealed to prefecture and county for twenty years without obtaining justice. When Hang arrived, he appealed again.
translations.idiomatic: The son had appealed to prefecture and county for twenty years without justice. When Hang arrived, he appealed again.

sentences.zh: 尹氏持積歲稅鈔為驗，沆曰：“若田千頃，歲輸豈特此耶？

translations.literal: The Yin clan produced tax receipts accumulated over years as proof. Hang said: "If the fields were a thousand qing, would the annual payment be only this much?"
translations.idiomatic: The Yin clan produced years of accumulated tax receipts as proof. Hang said: "If the fields were a thousand qing, would the annual tax be only this much?"

sentences.zh: 爾始為券時，嘗如敕問鄰乎？

translations.literal: When you first made the deed, did you question the neighbors as the edict requires?
translations.idiomatic: When you first made the deed, did you question the neighbors as the law requires?

sentences.zh: 其人固多在，可訊也。”

translations.literal: Those persons are surely still alive and can be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Those neighbors are surely still alive and can be questioned.

sentences.zh: 尹氏遂伏罪。

translations.literal: The Yin clan thereupon confessed their crime.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin clan thereupon confessed.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，曆三司度支、戶部判官、同修起居注，擢右正言、知制誥、判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, served in succession as commissioner of the Expenditure Section and Revenue Section of the Three Departments and as co-compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose, and was advanced to Right Remonstrator, drafter of edicts, and associate director of the Inner Stream Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, served as commissioner of the Three Departments' expenditure and revenue sections and co-compiler of the court diary, and was advanced to right remonstrator, edict drafter, and associate director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，館伴杜防強沆以酒，沆沾醉，拂袖起，因罵之，坐是出知潭州。

translations.literal: On a mission to Khitan, the host Du Fang pressed Hang with wine. Hang, half drunk, swept his sleeve and rose, and thereupon reviled him; for this he was sent out as prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Khitan, host Du Fang pressed him to drink. Half drunk, Hang swept his sleeve and rose, cursing Du Fang, and was posted out as prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又降知和州，改右諫議大夫、知江州。

translations.literal: He was demoted again to prefect of Hezhou, then changed to Right Censor-in-Chief and prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again to prefect of Hezhou, then made right censor-in-chief and prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時湖南蠻徭數出寇，至殺官吏。

translations.literal: At that time the Man and Yao of Hunan repeatedly raided, even killing officials.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Man and Yao of Hunan raided repeatedly, even killing officials.

sentences.zh: 以沆為龍圖閣直學士、知潭州兼安撫使，許便宜從事。

translations.literal: Hang was made Dragon Diagram Hall academician, prefect of Tanzhou with concurrent duty as pacification commissioner, and permitted to act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Hang was made Dragon Diagram Hall academician, prefect of Tanzhou and pacification commissioner, with authority to act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 沆大發兵至桂陽，招降二千餘人，使散居所部，而蠻酋降者皆奏命以官。

translations.literal: Hang mobilized a large force to Guiyang, induced more than two thousand to surrender, and had them disperse to their districts; chieftains of the Man who submitted were all memorialized for appointment to office.
translations.idiomatic: Hang mobilized a large force to Guiyang, induced more than two thousand to surrender and disperse to their districts, and memorialized for official appointments every Man chieftain who submitted.

sentences.zh: 又募土兵分捕餘黨，破桃油平、能家源，斬馘甚眾。

translations.literal: He also recruited local militia to hunt down the remnant bands in separate parties, broke Taoyouping and Nengjiayuan, and beheaded many.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited local militia to hunt down remnant bands, overran Taoyouping and Nengjiayuan, and beheaded many.

sentences.zh: 已而賊復出，殺裨將胡元，坐降知鄂州，徙京南，遷給事中，徙洪州。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits came out again and killed the assistant general Hu Yuan. Hang was demoted to prefect of Ezhou for this, transferred to Jingnan, promoted to Attendant Censor, and transferred to Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bandits reappeared and killed assistant general Hu Yuan. Hang was demoted to prefect of Ezhou, transferred to Jingnan, promoted to attendant censor, and transferred to Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，知審刑院，除知永興軍。

translations.literal: On his return he was made head of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed military prefect of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he headed the Court of Judicial Review and was appointed military prefect of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以龍圖閣學士權知開封府，數發隱伏。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, as Dragon Diagram Hall academician he was given acting charge of Kaifengfu and repeatedly uncovered hidden wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, as Dragon Diagram Hall academician he was given acting charge of Kaifeng and repeatedly uncovered hidden crimes.

sentences.zh: 祀明堂，遷尚書工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was sacrificed to, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the Bright Hall sacrifice he was promoted to vice director of works in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 逾年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: More than a year later he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時中書可否多用例，人或援例以訟，而法有不行。

translations.literal: At the time the Secretariat often used precedents to approve or reject matters; people would cite precedents in litigation, while statutes went unenforced.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat then relied heavily on precedent; litigants cited precedents while statutes went unenforced.

sentences.zh: 沆進言三弊曰：“近臣保薦辟請，動逾數十，皆浮薄權豪之流交相薦舉。

translations.literal: Hang submitted a memorial on three abuses, saying: "Recommendations and special appointments by those close to the throne often exceed several dozen at a time, all among the frivolous and powerful who recommend one another."
translations.idiomatic: Hang memorialized on three abuses: "Court favorites' recommendations and special appointments often number dozens at a time, all among the frivolous and powerful trading favors."

sentences.zh: 有司以之貿易，而遂使省、府、台、閣華資要職，路分、監司邊防寄任，授非公選，多出私門。

translations.literal: The relevant offices trade in these posts, so that splendid posts in the provinces, prefectures, censorate, and academies, circuit commissions, supervisory posts, and frontier trusts are given not by public selection but mostly through private channels.
translations.idiomatic: Offices traded in these posts, so splendid provincial, censorial, and academic posts, circuit commissions, and frontier trusts were filled not by public selection but through private patronage.

sentences.zh: 又職掌吏人遷補有常，而或減選出官、超資換職、堂除便家、先次差遣之類。

translations.literal: Moreover, clerks and functionaries have fixed rules for promotion and appointment, yet there are cases of reducing the selection quota for outgoing officials, advancing rank beyond qualification, changing posts by palace appointment for convenience, and preferential dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and functionaries had fixed promotion rules, yet posts were filled by cutting selection quotas, advancing rank beyond qualification, palace appointments for convenience, and preferential dispatch.

sentences.zh: 此近臣保薦之弊一也。

translations.literal: This is the first abuse of recommendations by those close to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: This was the first abuse of court favorites' recommendations.

sentences.zh: 審官、吏部銓、三班當入川、廣，乃求近地，當入近地，又求在京，及堂除升陟省府、館職、檢討之類。

translations.literal: Those due for assignment to Sichuan or Guang through the Court of Review, the Ministry of Personnel board, or the Three Classes would seek nearby posts; those due for nearby posts would seek the capital; and there were palace appointments to rise to provincial posts, academy posts, and editorial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Those due for Sichuan or Guang through review boards would seek nearby posts; those due for nearby posts would seek the capital; and palace appointments advanced men to provincial, academic, and editorial posts.

sentences.zh: 此近臣陳匄親屬之弊二也。

translations.literal: This is the second abuse of court favorites pleading for relatives.
translations.idiomatic: This was the second abuse of court favorites pleading for relatives.

sentences.zh: 其敘錢穀管庫之勞、捕賊昭雪之賞，常格雖存，僥幸猶甚。

translations.literal: In recording merit for managing funds and storehouses or rewards for catching bandits and clearing cases, though regular standards remain, favoritism is still extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Though regular standards remained for rewarding fiscal service and crime-fighting, favoritism still ran rampant.

sentences.zh: 以法則輕，以例則厚，執政者不能持法，多以例與之。

translations.literal: By statute the reward would be light, by precedent heavy; those in power could not uphold the law and mostly granted rewards by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: By statute rewards were light, by precedent heavy; those in power could not uphold the law and mostly granted rewards by precedent.

sentences.zh: 此敘勞幹進之弊三也。

translations.literal: This is the third abuse of recording merit through lobbying.
translations.idiomatic: This was the third abuse of merit records won through lobbying.

sentences.zh: 願詔中書、樞密，凡三事毋用例，餘聽如舊。”

translations.literal: I request an edict to the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs that in these three matters precedents not be used, and that the rest follow the old practice."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs be ordered not to use precedents in these three matters, while the rest follow established practice.

sentences.zh: 事既施行，而眾頗不悅，尋如舊。

translations.literal: The measure was put into effect, but many were displeased, and before long things reverted to the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: The measure was enacted, but many were displeased, and before long practice reverted to the old ways.

sentences.zh: 文彥博、富弼復入為相。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi again entered office as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi again became chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 彥博為昭文館大學士，弼監修國史，沆遷兵部侍郎，位在弼下。

translations.literal: Yanbo was Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, Bi supervised compilation of the national history, and Hang was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of War, ranking below Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall, Bi supervised the national history, and Hang was made vice director of war, ranking below Bi.

sentences.zh: 論者以為非故事，由學士楊察之誤，乃帖麻改沆監修國史，弼為集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: Commentators held this was not precedent, owing to an error by Academician Yang Cha; an edict on hemp paper was posted changing Hang to supervisor of the national history and Bi to Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held this broke precedent, owing to an error by academician Yang Cha; an edict was posted making Hang supervisor of the national history and Bi grand academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

sentences.zh: 沆既疾言事官，因言：“自慶曆後，台諫官用事，朝廷命令之出，事無當否悉論之，必勝而後已，專務抉人陰私莫辨之事，以中傷士大夫。

translations.literal: Hang, who already disliked remonstrating officials, thereupon said: "Since the Qingli era, censorial and remonstrance officials have wielded power. Whenever an order issued from court, whether right or wrong they debated it and would not stop until they won, specializing in dredging up unverifiable private matters to wound scholar-officials."
translations.idiomatic: Hang, who already disliked remonstrating officials, said: "Since the Qingli era censors and remonstrators have wielded power. Every court order, right or wrong, they debate until they win, dredging up unverifiable private matters to wound scholar-officials."

sentences.zh: 執政畏其言，進擢尤速。”

translations.literal: Those in power feared their words and promoted them with especial speed."
translations.idiomatic: Those in power feared their words and promoted them all the faster.

sentences.zh: 沆遂舉行御史遷次之格，滿二歲者與知州。

translations.literal: Hang thereupon implemented the regulation for censors' rotation: those who had served two full years were given prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Hang then implemented the censors' rotation rule: those who had served two full years were given prefectures.

sentences.zh: 御史范師道、趙抃歲滿求補郡，沆引格出之，中丞張等言沆挾私出御史。

translations.literal: The censors Fan Shidao and Zhao Bian, their terms complete, sought prefectural posts; Hang cited the regulation to send them out. The vice censor Zhang Deng and others said Hang was sending out censors from private motives.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Fan Shidao and Zhao Bian, their terms complete, sought prefectural posts; Hang cited the regulation to post them out. Vice censor Zhang Deng and others charged that Hang was acting from private motives.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使狄青亦因御史言，罷知陳州，沆奏曰：“御史去陛下將相，削陛下爪牙，此曹所謀，臣莫測也。”

translations.literal: At the time the Commissioner of Military Affairs Di Qing also, because of censorial talk, was dismissed to Chenzhou. Hang memorialized: "The censors are removing Your Majesty's generals and ministers and paring Your Majesty's claws and teeth—the designs of this lot, your servant cannot fathom."
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs commissioner Di Qing had also been dismissed to Chenzhou on censorial complaint. Hang memorialized: "The censors are stripping Your Majesty of generals and ministers and paring Your Majesty's claws and teeth—I cannot fathom what this faction is plotting."

sentences.zh: 升等益論辨不已，罷沆為觀文殿大學士、工部尚書、知應天府。

translations.literal: Deng and the others argued back ever more vigorously without cease, and Hang was dismissed to Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, Minister of Works, and prefect of Yingtianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng and the others argued on without cease, and Hang was dismissed to grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, minister of works, and prefect of Yingtianfu.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，徙陳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments and moved to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of punishments and posted to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 沆長於吏事，性豪率，少儀矩。

translations.literal: Hang was skilled in administrative affairs, bold and forthright by nature, and little given to ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Hang was skilled in administration, bold and forthright by nature, and little given to ceremony.

sentences.zh: 然任數，善刺探權近過失，陰持之以軒輊取事，論者以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he trusted to stratagem, was adept at probing the faults of those in power close to the throne, and secretly held these over them to tip the scales in affairs; commentators for this reason thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he trusted to stratagem, probed the faults of powerful courtiers, and secretly used them to tip affairs his way; critics thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左僕射兼侍中。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously given Left Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made left vice director of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 知制誥張瑰草詞詆沆，其家不敢請諡。

translations.literal: The edict drafter Zhang Gui drafted the eulogy slandering Hang, and his family did not dare request a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Edict drafter Zhang Gui drafted the eulogy in terms that slandered Hang, and his family did not dare request a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 帝為篆墓碑曰“思賢之碑”。

translations.literal: The emperor inscribed his tomb stele "Stele in Memory of the Worthy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inscribed his tomb stele "Stele in Memory of the Worthy."

sentences.zh: 子瑾，嘗為天章閣待制，坐法免，後以功復職。

translations.literal: His son Jin had once been Hanlin academician awaiting appointment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation; he was dismissed for violating the law but later restored to office for merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin had once been Hanlin academician of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation; he was dismissed for a legal offense but later restored for merit.

sentences.zh: 馮拯，字道濟。

translations.literal: Feng Zheng, styled Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zheng, courtesy name Daoji.

sentences.zh: 父俊，事漢湘陰公劉贇。

translations.literal: His father Jun served Liu Chong, Duke of Xiangyin of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun served Liu Chong, Duke of Xiangyin of Han.

sentences.zh: 贇死，俊與從行千餘人繫侍衛獄，周太祖赦出之，授檢校太子賓客，戍安遠軍馭馬鎮，辭不行，因徙居河陽。

translations.literal: When Chong died, Jun and more than a thousand who had followed him were imprisoned in the guard prison. Emperor Taizu of Zhou pardoned and released them, appointed Jun Honorary Guest of the Heir Apparent, and ordered him to garrison Yuma Town in Anyuan Army; he declined and moved to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong died, Jun and more than a thousand followers were imprisoned in the guard prison. Zhou Taizu pardoned them, appointed Jun honorary guest of the heir apparent, and ordered him to garrison Yuma Town in Anyuan Army; he declined and moved to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 拯以書生謁趙普，普奇其狀，曰：“子富貴壽考，宜不下我。”

translations.literal: Zheng as a scholar called on Zhao Pu; Pu was struck by his appearance and said, "You will enjoy wealth, honor, and long life—you should rank no lower than I."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng as a young scholar called on Zhao Pu; Pu was struck by his bearing and said, "You will enjoy wealth, honor, and long life—you should rank no lower than I."

sentences.zh: 舉進士，補大理評事、通判峽州，權知澤州，徙坊州，遷太常丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Reviewing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review and supervisory prefect of Xiazhou, given acting charge of Zezhou, transferred to Fangzhou, and promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as reviewing clerk of the Court of Judicial Review and supervisory prefect of Xiazhou, acted as prefect of Zezhou, transferred to Fangzhou, and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 江南旱，命馳傳振貸貧乏，察官吏能否，還奏稱旨，權知石州，擢右正言，歲餘代歸。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan suffered drought, he was ordered by express relay to relieve the poor with loans, inspect officials' competence, and on his return memorialized to the emperor's satisfaction; he was given acting charge of Shizhou, promoted to Right Remonstrator, and after more than a year was replaced and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan suffered drought he was sent by express relay to lend grain to the poor and inspect officials' competence; his memorial pleased the emperor. He acted as prefect of Shizhou, was promoted to right remonstrator, and after a year was replaced and recalled.

sentences.zh: 出使河北，與轉運使樊知古計邊儲，還，判三司戶部理欠憑由司，為度支判官。

translations.literal: On a mission to Hebei he planned frontier stores with transport commissioner Fan Zhigu; on his return he was assigned to the Three Departments' Revenue Section office for clearing arrears vouchers and made commissioner of the Expenditure Section.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Hebei he planned frontier stores with transport commissioner Fan Zhigu; on his return he headed the Three Departments' arrears office and became expenditure commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，有上封請立皇太子者，拯與尹黃裳、王世則、洪湛伏閣請立許王元僖，太宗怒，悉貶嶺外。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era someone submitted a sealed memorial requesting establishment of a crown prince. Zheng, Yin Huangshang, Wang Shize, and Hong Zhan lay prostrate at the gate requesting installation of Prince Xu Yuanxi; Taizong was angry and all were banished beyond the Ling.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunhua era someone submitted a sealed memorial requesting a crown prince. Zheng, Yin Huangshang, Wang Shize, and Hong Zhan lay prostrate at the gate demanding Prince Xu Yuanxi be named heir; Taizong was furious and banished them all beyond the Ling.

sentences.zh: 拯知端州，既至，上言請遣使括諸路隱丁、更製版籍及議鹽法通商，凡十餘事。

translations.literal: Zheng was made prefect of Duanzhou; on arrival he memorialized requesting envoys to survey hidden households on all circuits, revise the household registers, and discuss opening salt trade, more than ten matters in all.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was made prefect of Duanzhou; on arrival he memorialized requesting envoys to survey hidden households on all circuits, revise registers, and discuss opening the salt trade—more than ten proposals in all.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲召還參知政事，寇準素不悅拯，乃徙知鼎州。

translations.literal: Taizong wished to recall him as Vice Grand Councilor, but Kou Zhun had never liked Zheng and had him transferred to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wished to recall him as vice grand councilor, but Kou Zhun, who disliked Zheng, had him transferred to Dingzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 改通判廣州。

translations.literal: He was changed to supervisory prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervisory prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 郊祀畢，覃恩，拯與通判彭惟節皆遷尚書員外郎，惟節以太常博士為屯田員外，而拯以左正言為虞部員外。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was completed and grace extended, Zheng and supervisory prefect Peng Weijie were both promoted to Vice Directors in the Secretariat; Weijie from Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to Vice Director of the Fields Section, and Zheng from Left Remonstrator to Vice Director of the Parks Section.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice and general amnesty, Zheng and supervisory prefect Peng Weijie were both promoted to vice directors in the Secretariat; Weijie from erudite of imperial sacrifices to vice director of the fields section, and Zheng from left remonstrator to vice director of the parks section.

sentences.zh: 拯書名舊在惟節上，及奏事如故，準切責之。

translations.literal: Zheng's name on memorials had formerly ranked above Weijie's, yet when presenting business he still did so as before; Kou Zhun sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's name had formerly ranked above Weijie's on memorials, yet he still presented business as before; Kou Zhun sharply rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 拯上書言準阿意不平，準坐此罷。

translations.literal: Zheng submitted a memorial saying Zhun was partial and unfair; Zhun was dismissed on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng memorialized that Zhun was partial and unfair; Zhun was dismissed on this account.

sentences.zh: 拯以母喪請內徙，命知江州。

translations.literal: Zheng, on his mother's death, requested transfer inland and was appointed prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, mourning his mother, requested transfer inland and was appointed prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，進比部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was advanced to Vice Director of the Comptroller Section.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded he was promoted to vice director of the comptroller section.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞李惟清表為推直官，判三司度支勾院，遷駕部。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Weiqing recommended him as investigating commissioner; he was assigned to the Three Departments' Expenditure Section audit office and promoted to the Chariot Section.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Li Weiqing recommended him as investigating commissioner; he headed the Three Departments' expenditure audit office and was promoted to the chariot section.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，坐試開封進士賦涉譏訕，下拯御史台，未幾，釋之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianping era, because the fu composition in testing Kaifeng jinshi candidates involved satire, Zheng was sent to the Censorate; before long he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping era, because the fu composition in testing Kaifeng jinshi candidates involved satire, Zheng was sent to the Censorate; he was soon released.

sentences.zh: 明年，兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: The next year he was made concurrent Attending Censor with miscellaneous duties.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made concurrent attending censor with miscellaneous duties.

sentences.zh: 時西北用兵，王超、傅潛將兵出定、瀛間，觀望玩寇，拯極論之，不報。

translations.literal: At the time the northwest was at war; Wang Chao and Fu Qian led troops out between Ding and Ying, watching and toying with the enemy. Zheng argued strenuously against this, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest was at war; Wang Chao and Fu Qian led troops out between Ding and Ying, watching and toying with the enemy. Zheng argued strenuously but received no response.

sentences.zh: 超等果逗撓覆軍。

translations.literal: Chao and the others indeed delayed and lost their army.
translations.idiomatic: Chao and the others indeed delayed and lost their army.

sentences.zh: 命拯按傅獄，抵潛罪，竄流之。

translations.literal: Zheng was ordered to investigate Fu's case, found Qian guilty, and had him banished.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was ordered to investigate Fu's case, found Qian guilty, and had him banished.

sentences.zh: 擢祠部郎中、樞密直學士，權判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Sacrificial Section and Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, with acting charge of the Inner Stream Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the sacrificial section and academician directly attached to military affairs, with acting charge of personnel.

sentences.zh: 以審官及銓法未備，建請凡蔭補京官，試讀一經，書家狀通習為中格，始得仕。

translations.literal: Because the Court of Review and appointment regulations were incomplete, he proposed that all who entered capital office by privilege must be tested in reading one classic and writing a family biography showing mastery as the passing standard before they could take office.
translations.idiomatic: Because review and appointment regulations were incomplete, he proposed that all who entered capital office by privilege must pass a test in reading one classic and writing a family biography showing mastery.

sentences.zh: 同勾當三班院。

translations.literal: He concurrently handled affairs in the Three Classes Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently handled affairs in the Three Classes Bureau.

sentences.zh: 向敏中宣撫河北、河東，拯及陳堯叟為副，宴餞長春殿。

translations.literal: Xiang Minzhong was pacification commissioner for Hebei and Hedong; Zheng and Chen Yaosou served as his deputies, and a farewell banquet was held in the Hall of Everlasting Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Minzhong was pacification commissioner for Hebei and Hedong; Zheng and Chen Yaosou served as his deputies, with a farewell banquet in the Hall of Everlasting Spring.

sentences.zh: 明年，以右諫議大夫同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Right Censor-in-Chief and Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made right censor-in-chief and associate commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝欲修綏州，謀諸輔臣，拯與宰相向敏中等皆曰便。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to repair Suizhou and consulted the chief ministers; Zheng and the chief minister Xiang Minzhong and others all said it was expedient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to repair Suizhou and consulted his ministers; Zheng and chief minister Xiang Minzhong and others all said it was expedient.

sentences.zh: 宰相呂蒙正、參知政事王旦、王欽若皆曰宜棄勿修。

translations.literal: The chief ministers Lü Mengzheng and Vice Grand Councilors Wang Dan and Wang Qinruo all said it should be abandoned and not repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Lü Mengzheng and vice grand councilors Wang Dan and Wang Qinruo all said it should be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝遣洪湛馳驛往視，還，上七利二害，卒修完之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Hong Zhan by express relay to inspect; on his return he submitted seven advantages and two disadvantages, and in the end the repairs were completed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Hong Zhan by express relay to inspect; he returned with seven advantages and two disadvantages listed, and the repairs were completed.

sentences.zh: 時上封者言：“三司多滯務，州郡稟疑事，吏民訴理冤獄，依違不決者輒數歲，水旱或由於此。”

translations.literal: At the time a sealed memorialist said: "The Three Departments have many delayed matters; when prefectures and commanderies report doubtful cases and officials and commoners appeal to settle unjust lawsuits, indecision often lasts several years—drought and flood may stem from this."
translations.idiomatic: A sealed memorialist said: "The Three Departments delay many matters; when prefectures report doubtful cases and people appeal unjust lawsuits, indecision often lasts years—drought and flood may stem from this."

sentences.zh: 詔拯選幹強吏同三司使裁冗事、督舉稽留，遂與判度支勾院孫冕省帳牘二十一萬五千本，並廢冗官十五員。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zheng to select capable strong officials to join the Three Departments commissioners in cutting redundant business and pressing delayed matters; he and Sun Mian of the Expenditure Section audit office reviewed 215,000 account documents and abolished fifteen redundant posts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zheng to select capable officials to join the Three Departments commissioners in cutting redundancy and pressing delays; with expenditure auditor Sun Mian he reviewed 215,000 account documents and abolished fifteen redundant posts.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書工部侍郎、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat and given signing authority in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of works and given signing authority in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 賜手劄訪邊事，拯謂：“備邊之要，不扼險以制敵之衝，未易勝也。

translations.literal: He was granted an autograph note inquiring about frontier affairs. Zheng said: "The essential in frontier defense is to hold the passes and control the enemy's thrust—otherwise victory is not easy."
translations.idiomatic: He received an autograph note inquiring about frontier affairs. Zheng said: "Frontier defense depends on holding the passes to control the enemy's thrust—otherwise victory is difficult."

sentences.zh: 若於保州、威虜間，依徐、鮑河為陣，其表勢可取勝矣。

translations.literal: If between Baozhou and Weilu one arrays forces along the Xu and Bao rivers, the outward disposition can secure victory.
translations.idiomatic: If between Baozhou and Weilu forces were arrayed along the Xu and Bao rivers, the outward disposition could secure victory.

sentences.zh: 前歲王顯違詔不趨要地，契丹初壓境，王師未行，而契丹騎已入鈔，賴霖雨乃遁去。

translations.literal: The year before, Wang Xian disobeyed the edict and did not hurry to the vital point. When Khitan first pressed the border, the imperial army had not marched, yet Khitan cavalry had already raided in; they escaped only thanks to heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, Wang Xian disobeyed the edict and failed to reach the vital point. When Khitan first pressed the border the imperial army had not marched, yet Khitan cavalry had already raided in—they escaped only thanks to heavy rain.

sentences.zh: 比王超奏敵已去，而東路奏敵方來，既聚軍中山以救望都，而兵困糧匱，將臣陷歿幾盡，超等僅以身免。

translations.literal: When Wang Chao reported the enemy had gone, the eastern route reported the enemy was still coming. Troops were massed at Zhongshan to rescue Wangdu, but the army was exhausted and provisions scarce; generals and ministers were nearly all lost, and Chao and the others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chao reported the enemy had gone, the eastern route reported they were still coming. Troops massed at Zhongshan to rescue Wangdu, but the army was exhausted and provisions scarce; generals and ministers were nearly all lost, and Chao and the others barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 今防秋，宜於唐河增屯兵至六萬，控定武之北為大陣，邢州置都總管為中陣，天雄軍置鈐轄為後陣，罷莫州狼山兩路兵。”

translations.literal: Now for autumn defense, troops at the Tang River should be increased to sixty thousand; north of Dingwu should be the great array, Xingzhou should have an overall commander as the middle array, Tianxiong Army a controller as the rear array, and the two-route forces of Mozhou and Langshan should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For autumn defense he proposed increasing Tang River garrisons to sixty thousand, a great array north of Dingwu, an overall commander at Xingzhou as the middle array, a controller at Tianxiong Army as the rear array, and abolishing the two-route forces of Mozhou and Langshan.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: This was adopted.

sentences.zh: 景德中，為參知政事，再遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era he was made Vice Grand Councilor and again promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde era he was made vice grand councilor and again promoted to vice director of war.

sentences.zh: 攝事享太廟，有司供帳幔，守奉人宿廟室前，喧囂不肅，拯以聞。

translations.literal: Acting in the sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the relevant offices supplied curtains; the attendants lodged before the temple chambers, noisy and disorderly. Zheng reported this.
translations.idiomatic: While acting at the Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifice, attendants lodged before the temple chambers in noisy disorder. Zheng reported it.

sentences.zh: 詔專為廟享製帟幕什器，藏宗正寺，禁吏卒登廟階。

translations.literal: An edict ordered curtains and utensils made solely for temple sacrifices, stored in the Court of the Imperial Clan, and forbade clerks and soldiers to ascend the temple steps.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered curtains and utensils made solely for temple sacrifices, stored in the Court of the Imperial Clan, and forbade clerks and soldiers on the temple steps.

sentences.zh: 王濟上編敕，帝以其煩簡不一，語輔臣曰：“顯德敕尤煩，蓋世宗嚴急，出於一時之意，臣下不敢言其失也。”

translations.literal: Wang Ji submitted a compiled code of statutes; the emperor, finding it cumbersome and inconsistent, told the chief ministers: "The Xiande statutes were especially cumbersome, for Shizong was severe and urgent and acted from momentary impulse—his subjects dared not speak of the faults."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji submitted a compiled code; the emperor, finding it cumbersome and inconsistent, told his ministers: "The Xiande statutes were especially cumbersome—Shizong was severe and acted on impulse, and his subjects dared not speak of the faults."

sentences.zh: 王旦進曰：“詔敕宜簡，近亦傷於煩。”

translations.literal: Wang Dan advanced and said: "Edicts and commands should be concise; recently they have also suffered from being cumbersome."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said: "Edicts should be concise; recently they have also grown cumbersome."

sentences.zh: 拯對曰：“開寶間，除諸州通判敕，刑獄、錢穀悉條列約束，今則略矣。”

translations.literal: Zheng replied: "In the Kaibao era, when appointing supervisory prefects for the various prefectures, the edicts listed constraints on criminal cases and funds in full detail—now they are abbreviated."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied: "In the Kaibao era edicts appointing supervisory prefects listed criminal and fiscal constraints in full detail—now they are abbreviated."

sentences.zh: 時契丹始盟，拯言邊方騷動，武臣幸之以為利。

translations.literal: At the time Khitan had just made alliance; Zheng said the frontier was unsettled and military officials took advantage of this for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan had just made alliance; Zheng said the frontier was unsettled and military officials profited from it.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“朝廷以信為守，然戒備不可廢也，此外，當靜治以安吾民爾。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The court takes trust as its guard, yet vigilance cannot be abandoned. Beyond this, we should govern quietly to settle our people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The court takes trust as its guard, yet vigilance cannot be abandoned. Beyond that we should govern quietly to settle our people."

sentences.zh: 爾其奉承之。”

translations.literal: You should carry this out.
translations.idiomatic: Carry this out.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，嚴貢舉糊名法。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong Xiangfu era, the sealed-name method for examinations was strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era the sealed-name method for examinations was strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 拯與王旦論選舉帝前，拯請兼考策論，不專以詩賦為進退。

translations.literal: Zheng and Wang Dan discussed selection before the emperor; Zheng requested that policy essays be tested together and that advancement not depend solely on poetry and fu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Wang Dan discussed selection before the emperor; Zheng asked that policy essays be tested and advancement not depend solely on poetry and fu.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“可以觀才識者，文論也。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What can reveal talent and insight is the policy essay."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Policy essays reveal talent and insight."

sentences.zh: 拯論事多合帝意如此。

translations.literal: Zheng's discussions of affairs often accorded with the emperor's intent in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's counsel often accorded with the emperor's intent in this way.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，為儀仗使。

translations.literal: When Mount Tai was enfeoffed, he was made commissioner of ceremonial guards.
translations.idiomatic: For the Mount Tai feng sacrifice he was made commissioner of ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 禮成，進尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was advanced to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed he was promoted to left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以疾在告，數請罷，帝以手詔諭旨，又命宰相王旦就第勸拯起視事。

translations.literal: Ill, he reported leave and repeatedly requested dismissal; the emperor sent an autograph note of instruction and ordered the chief minister Wang Dan to visit his residence to urge Zheng to rise and attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he repeatedly requested leave; the emperor sent an autograph note and ordered chief minister Wang Dan to visit his home to urge him back to duty.

sentences.zh: 從祀汾陰，為儀仗使，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: Following the sacrifice at Fenyin, he was made commissioner of ceremonial guards and transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Fenyin sacrifice he was made commissioner of ceremonial guards and promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 復以疾求罷，拜刑部尚書、知河南府，聽以府事委官屬。

translations.literal: Again ill, he sought dismissal and was appointed Minister of Punishments and prefect of Henanfu, permitted to entrust prefectural affairs to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Again ill, he sought dismissal and was made minister of punishments and prefect of Henan, permitted to entrust affairs to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 七年，除御史中丞，又以疾辭，除戶部尚書、知陳州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief; again pleading illness, he was made Minister of Revenue and prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made vice censor-in-chief; again pleading illness, he was made minister of revenue and prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗謂王旦曰：“拯固求閑郡，何邪？”

translations.literal: Zhenzong once said to Wang Dan: "Zheng keeps seeking a quiet prefecture—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong once asked Wang Dan: "Why does Zheng keep seeking a quiet prefecture?"

sentences.zh: 旦對曰：“馬知節嘗譏拯好富貴，所欲節度使爾。

translations.literal: Dan replied: "Ma Zhijie once mocked Zheng for loving wealth and honor—what he wants is to be a military commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Dan replied: "Ma Zhijie once mocked Zheng for loving wealth and honor—what he wants is a military commissioner's post.

sentences.zh: 拯恐為知節所量，不敢請大藩，殆為此也。”

translations.literal: Zheng fears being sized up by Zhijie and does not dare request a great prefecture—probably for this reason."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng fears being sized up by Zhijie and does not dare request a major prefecture—probably for that reason.

sentences.zh: 再知河南府，遷兵部尚書，入判尚書都省，以吏部尚書、檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事充樞密使。

translations.literal: Again made prefect of Henanfu, transferred to Minister of War, entered to preside over the Secretariat Directorate, and as Minister of Personnel, Honorary Grand Tutor, and Tongzhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi served as Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Again prefect of Henan, then minister of war, presiding over the secretariat directorate, and as minister of personnel, honorary grand tutor, and grand councilor he served as commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 其冬，拜右僕射兼中書侍郎、太子少傅、同平章事、集賢殿大學士，進左僕射。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Associate Grand Councilor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and advanced to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat with concurrent secretariat vice director, junior tutor of the heir apparent, associate grand councilor, and grand academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and advanced to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，進封魏國公，遷司空兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Wei and transferred to Minister of Works with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianxing he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei and made minister of works with concurrent appointment as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 輔臣會食資善堂，召議事，丁謂獨不預。

translations.literal: The chief ministers dined together in the Hall for Nurturing Goodness and were summoned to discuss affairs; Ding Wei alone was not included.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers dined in the Hall for Nurturing Goodness and were summoned to discuss affairs; Ding Wei alone was excluded.

sentences.zh: 謂知得罪，頗哀請。

translations.literal: Wei knew he had offended and pleaded piteously.
translations.idiomatic: Wei knew he had offended and pleaded piteously.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演遽曰：“當致力，無大憂也。”

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan hastily said: "You should exert yourself—there is no great worry."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan hastily said: "Exert yourself—there is no great worry."

sentences.zh: 拯熟視惟演，惟演踧踖。

translations.literal: Zheng stared fixedly at Weiyan, and Weiyan was abashed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng stared fixedly at Weiyan until Weiyan was abashed.

sentences.zh: 及對承明殿，太后怒甚，語欲誅謂。

translations.literal: When they faced audience in Chenming Hall, the empress dowager was greatly angry and spoke of wishing to execute Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At audience in Chenming Hall the empress dowager was furious and spoke of executing Wei.

sentences.zh: 拯進曰：“謂固有罪，然帝新即位，亟誅大臣，駭天下耳目。

translations.literal: Zheng stepped forward and said: "Wei indeed has guilt, yet the emperor has newly acceded to the throne; to execute a grand minister hastily would alarm the eyes and ears of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng stepped forward and said, "Wei is guilty, no doubt—but the emperor has only just taken the throne. To execute a senior minister so soon would shock the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 謂豈有逆謀哉？

translations.literal: How could Wei have had a treasonous plot?
translations.idiomatic: What treasonous plot could he possibly have had?

sentences.zh: 第失奏山陵事耳。”

translations.literal: It is only the offense of failing to report on the imperial tomb matter."
translations.idiomatic: His offense was merely failing to report on the imperial tomb."

sentences.zh: 太后怒少解。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's anger eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's rage subsided a little.

sentences.zh: 謂既貶，拯代謂為司徒、玉清昭應宮使、昭文館大學士、監修國史，又為山陵使，奉安真宗御容於西京。

translations.literal: After Wei was demoted, Zheng replaced him as Minister of Education, commissioner of the Jade Pure Temple of Illustrious Response, grand academician of the Hall for Propagation of Culture, and supervising editor of national history; he also served as commissioner for the imperial tomb, installing Emperor Zhenzong's portrait in the Western Capital.
