translations.idiomatic: Once Wei was demoted, Zheng succeeded to his posts as minister of education, commissioner of the Jade Pure Temple of Illustrious Response, grand academician of the Hall for Propagation of Culture, and supervising editor of national history. He also served as imperial tomb commissioner, installing Emperor Zhenzong's portrait in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 尋在病告，帝賜白金五千兩，拯叩頭稱謝。

translations.literal: Soon while on sick leave, the emperor bestowed five thousand taels of white silver; Zheng kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, while on medical leave, the emperor granted him five thousand taels of silver; Zheng kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 五上表願罷相，拜武勝軍節度使、檢校太尉兼侍中、判河南府。

translations.literal: Five times he submitted memorials requesting to resign the chancellorship; he was appointed military commissioner of Wusheng Army, honorary grand marshal concurrently palace secretariat director, and prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted five memorials asking to leave the chancellorship and was appointed military commissioner of Wusheng Army, honorary grand marshal and palace secretariat director, and prefect of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 即臥內賜告及旌纛，遣內司賓撫問。

translations.literal: Immediately from the inner chamber he was granted leave and command banners; an Inner Chamber Attendant was sent to convey concern.
translations.idiomatic: From the inner chamber the emperor immediately granted him leave and command pennants and sent an Inner Chamber Attendant to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 還，奏其家儉陋，被服甚質。

translations.literal: On returning, he memorialized that Zheng's household was frugal and modest and his dress and furnishings very plain.
translations.idiomatic: When the attendant returned, he reported that Zheng's home was spare and humble and his clothing and furnishings extremely plain.

sentences.zh: 太后賜以衾裯錦綺屏，然拯平居自奉侈靡，顧禁中不知也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager bestowed upon him quilts, brocade, and screens; yet Zheng in his daily private life maintained himself lavishly—only the forbidden precinct did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent him quilts, brocades, and screens—but in private life Zheng lived lavishly, a fact the palace never learned.

sentences.zh: 既卒，贈太師、中書令，諡文懿。

translations.literal: After he died, he was posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor and Grand Secretariat Director; his posthumous title was Wanyi.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made grand preceptor and grand secretariat director, with the posthumous name Wanyi.

sentences.zh: 拯氣貌嚴重，宦者傳詔至中書，不延坐。

translations.literal: Zheng's bearing and appearance were stern and dignified; when eunuchs came to the Secretariat to deliver edicts, he did not invite them to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was stern and imposing in bearing. When eunuchs arrived at the Secretariat to deliver edicts, he never offered them a seat.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書林特嘗詣第，累日不得通，白以諮事，使詣中書。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Lin Te once called at his residence; for many days he could not gain access. Te reported that he wished to consult on affairs and was told to go to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Lin Te once visited his home but could not get in for days. When Te said he had business to discuss, he was told to go to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既至，又遣堂吏謂之曰：“公事何不自達朝廷？”

translations.literal: When he arrived, Zheng again sent a hall clerk to tell him: "Why do you not take official business directly to the court yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: When Te arrived, Zheng sent a hall clerk to tell him, "Why don't you take official business straight to the court?"

sentences.zh: 卒不見，特大愧而去。

translations.literal: In the end he did not receive him; Te left in great shame.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Zheng refused to see him, and Te withdrew in deep humiliation.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演營入相，拯以太后姻家力言之，遂出惟演河陽。

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan schemed to enter the chancellorship; Zheng, as a relative by marriage of the empress dowager, spoke forcefully against it, and Weiyan was sent out to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Weiyan maneuvered for a seat in the chancellorship, Zheng—related to the empress dowager by marriage—argued forcefully against it, and Weiyan was posted out to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 子行己、伸己。

translations.literal: His sons Xingji and Shenji.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Xingji and Shenji.

translations.literal: 〈Sons〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sons〉

sentences.zh: 行己

translations.literal: Xingji
translations.idiomatic: Xingji

sentences.zh: 行己字肅之，以父任為右侍禁、涇原路駐泊都監、知憲州，因治狀增秩。

translations.literal: Xingji, styled Suzhi, entered office through his father's privilege as Right Palace Guard, Frontier Station Garrison Supervisor of Jingyuan Circuit and prefect of Xianzhou; for administrative merit his rank was raised.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji, courtesy name Suzhi, entered service through his father's privilege as a right palace guard, garrison supervisor on the Jingyuan frontier, and prefect of Xianzhou; his rank was raised for competent administration.

sentences.zh: 曆石、保、霸、冀、莫五州，所至有能稱。

translations.literal: He served in succession at the five prefectures of Shi, Bao, Ba, Ji, and Mo; wherever he went he won repute for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Shi, Bao, Ba, Ji, and Mo, earning a reputation for ability wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 夏人既納款，疆候播言契丹治兵幽燕，大為戰具，議者欲解西備北，行己言：“遼、夏為與國，元昊入貢，容懷詭計，幽燕治兵，或為虛聲，邊鄙之虞，恐不在河朔也。”

translations.literal: After the Xia people had submitted, frontier scouts spread word that the Khitan were drilling troops in Youyan and greatly preparing weapons of war; debaters wished to ease western defenses and strengthen the north. Xingji said: "Liao and Xia are allied states; Yuanhao's tribute may harbor crafty designs; troop preparations in Youyan may be empty bluster—the worries at the frontier borders, I fear, may not lie in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tangut submitted, frontier scouts reported that the Khitan were mobilizing in Youyan and stockpiling arms on a large scale, and some argued for easing defenses in the west to reinforce the north. Xingji said, "Liao and Xia are allied. Yuanhao's tribute may conceal a trick; Khitan troop movements in Youyan may be bluff. I suspect the real danger on the frontier may not lie in Hebei at all.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，知定州，韓琦薦為路鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era he was prefect of Dingzhou; Han Qi recommended him as circuit supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era he served as prefect of Dingzhou; Han Qi recommended him as circuit supervisory commissioner.

sentences.zh: 徙知代州，管幹河東緣邊安撫事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Daizhou and directed frontier pacification affairs along eastern Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Daizhou and put in charge of frontier pacification along the eastern Hedong border.

sentences.zh: 夏人掠麟州，蕃部且盜耕屈野河西田，遇官軍逴邏者，輒聚射。

translations.literal: Xia raiders plundered Linzhou; tribal groups also illicitly cultivated fields west of the Quye River, and whenever they encountered government patrols they would gather to shoot at them.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut raiders plundered Linzhou, and tribal groups were also farming illegally west of the Quye River; whenever they met government patrols they would mass and shoot.

sentences.zh: 詔行己計之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xingji to plan a response.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Xingji to devise a response.

sentences.zh: 行己言：“此奸民無忌憚，非君長過，不宜以細故啟大釁，但加戒戢足矣。”

translations.literal: Xingji said: "These are lawless people without restraint; it is not a fault of their chieftains. One should not provoke a major quarrel over a small matter—strengthening discipline and restraint is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji said, "These are unruly people acting without fear—it is not the fault of their chiefs. We should not start a major conflict over a minor matter. Stronger discipline will suffice.

sentences.zh: 五台山寺調廂兵義勇繕葺，為除和糴穀三萬，行己謂不可損歲入之儲，以事不急之務。

translations.literal: Mount Wutai temples conscripted garrison militia and volunteers for repairs and sought exemption from thirty thousand units of he-qu grain levies; Xingji held that one must not deplete annual revenue reserves for non-urgent business.
translations.idiomatic: Temples on Mount Wutai conscripted garrison troops and volunteers for repairs and sought exemption from thirty thousand units of government grain purchases. Xingji argued that annual revenue reserves should not be drained for non-urgent work.

sentences.zh: 進西上閣門使，四遷客省使，更高陽關、秦鳳、定州、大名府路馬步總管，以衛州防禦使致仕，預洛陽耆英之集。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Western Upper Gate envoy, four times promoted to Guest Reception envoy, then further to overall cavalry and infantry commander of Gaoyang Pass, Qin-Feng, Dingzhou, and Daming prefectural circuits; he retired as Defender of Weizhou and joined the gathering of venerable elders at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Western Upper Gate envoy, was promoted four times to Guest Reception envoy, and then served as overall cavalry and infantry commander on the Gaoyang Pass, Qin-Feng, Dingzhou, and Daming circuits. He retired as defender of Weizhou and took part in the gathering of venerable elders at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，終金州觀察使，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he died as military observer of Jinzhou, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era he died in office as military observer of Jinzhou, at the age of eighty-four.

translations.literal: 〈Sons〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sons〉

sentences.zh: 伸己

translations.literal: Shenji
translations.idiomatic: Shenji

sentences.zh: 伸己字齊賢，以蔭補右侍禁。

translations.literal: Shenji, styled Qixian, entered office by privilege as Right Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji, courtesy name Qixian, entered service by privilege as a right palace guard.

sentences.zh: 累遷西頭供奉官，授閣門祗候、桂州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Western Head Palace Attendant, appointed Gate Lieutenant and military commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts to Western Head Palace Attendant and was appointed gate lieutenant and military commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 轉運使俞獻可辟知廉州。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Yu Xiankai recruited him as prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Yu Xiankai appointed him prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，安化蠻擾邊，獻可又薦知宜州。

translations.literal: After a long time, when the Anhua barbarians harassed the frontier, Xiankai again recommended him as prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Anhua tribes raided the frontier, Xiankai again recommended him as prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，改桂、宜、融、柳、象沿邊兵馬都監，遂專溪峒事。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era he was changed to frontier military commander along Gui, Yi, Rong, Liu, and Xiang and henceforth specialized in Stream-Gorge affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiansheng era he became frontier military commander for Gui, Yi, Rong, Liu, and Xiang and thereafter specialized in stream-gorge affairs.

sentences.zh: 以禮賓使復知宜州。

translations.literal: As Protocol Reception Commissioner he again became prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As protocol reception commissioner he again served as prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 代還，道改供備庫使、知邕州。

translations.literal: On returning from a replacement tour, en route he was changed to Storehouse Equipment Commissioner and prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back after completing a tour of duty, he was reassigned en route to storehouse equipment commissioner and prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 治舍有井，相傳不敢飲，飲輒死。

translations.literal: His official residence had a well; tradition held that no one dared drink from it—whoever drank would die.
translations.idiomatic: His official residence had a well that local lore said was deadly—anyone who drank from it would die.

sentences.zh: 伸己日汲自供，終更無恙。

translations.literal: Shenji drew water daily for his own use and completed his term without harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji drew from it every day for his own use and finished his term unharmed.

sentences.zh: 旁城數里，有金花木，土俗言花開即瘴起，人不敢近。

translations.literal: Several li outside the city wall were golden-flower trees; local custom said when the flowers bloomed miasma would rise, and people dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: A few li outside the city stood golden-flower trees; local custom held that when they bloomed miasma would rise, and no one dared go near.

sentences.zh: 伸己故以花盛時酣燕其下，亦復無害。

translations.literal: Shenji deliberately held a banquet beneath them when the flowers were in full bloom and likewise suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji deliberately held a feast beneath them at the height of bloom and suffered no ill effects.

sentences.zh: 明道恭謝，改東染院使、領榮州刺史、梓夔路兵馬鈐轄，遷洛苑使、知桂州兼廣西鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the Mingdao thanksgiving ceremony he was changed to Eastern Dyeing Commissioner, concurrently prefect of Rongzhou and cavalry and infantry supervisory commissioner of the Zi-Cui circuit; he was transferred to Luoyuan Commissioner and prefect of Guizhou concurrently with Guangxi supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the Mingdao thanksgiving ceremony he was made Eastern Dyeing Commissioner, prefect of Rongzhou, and cavalry and infantry supervisory commissioner of the Zi-Cui circuit, then promoted to Luoyuan commissioner, prefect of Guizhou, and Guangxi supervisory commissioner.

sentences.zh: 道江陵，會安化蠻犯邊，官軍不利，仁宗遣中人趣伸己討之。

translations.literal: Passing Jiangling, he happened upon Anhua barbarians invading the frontier; the government army fared poorly. Renzong sent a court envoy to urge Shenji to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Jiangling, he learned that the Anhua tribes had invaded the frontier and the government forces were faring badly. Renzong sent a palace envoy to hurry Shenji to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 伸己日夜疾馳至宜州，繕器甲，募丁壯，轉糧餉，由三路以進。

translations.literal: Shenji galloped day and night to Yizhou, repaired armor and weapons, recruited strong youths, moved grain supplies, and advanced by three routes.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji raced day and night to Yizhou, repaired arms and armor, recruited able-bodied men, moved supplies, and advanced by three routes.

sentences.zh: 伸己臨軍，單騎出陣，語酋豪曰：“朝廷撫汝甚厚，汝乃自取滅亡耶！

translations.literal: Shenji came before the army, rode out alone to the battle line, and said to the tribal chiefs: "The court has treated you very generously—will you yet bring ruin upon yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Shenji came before the army, rode out alone to the enemy line, and addressed the tribal chiefs: "The court has treated you generously—will you bring destruction on yourselves?

sentences.zh: 今我奉天子命來，汝聽吾言則生，不則無噍類矣。”

translations.literal: Now I come bearing the Son of Heaven's command; heed my words and you live—otherwise not one of you will remain alive."
translations.idiomatic: I come now on the Son of Heaven's orders. Heed me and live; refuse, and not one of you will survive."

sentences.zh: 眾仰泣羅拜曰：“不圖今日再見馮公也。”

translations.literal: The multitude looked up weeping and bowed in prostration, saying: "We never dreamed we would see Lord Feng again today."
translations.idiomatic: The crowd looked up, weeping, and prostrated themselves, saying, "We never thought we would see Lord Feng again."

sentences.zh: 明日，蠻渠棄兵械率眾降軍門。

translations.literal: The next day the barbarian leaders cast away weapons and led the masses to surrender at the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the tribal leaders cast down their arms and led their followers to surrender at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 初，部卒以覆將畏匿，伸己曰：“紀律不明，主將也，戰士何罪？”

translations.literal: Initially, troops had hidden out of fear because the defeated general had fled. Shenji said: "When discipline is unclear, the fault lies with the commanding general—what crime do the soldiers bear?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, soldiers had hidden because their routed commander had fled in fear. Shenji said, "When discipline breaks down, the fault is the commander's—what crime did the rank and file commit?"

sentences.zh: 請於朝，貸其死。

translations.literal: He requested of the court and their death sentences were commuted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the court and had their death sentences commuted.

sentences.zh: 以勞遷西上閣門使、知宜州。

translations.literal: For his labors he was transferred to Western Upper Gate envoy and prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Western Upper Gate envoy and prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 樂善蠻寇武陽，伸己遣諭禍福，蠻大悅，悉還所掠。

translations.literal: When the Leshan barbarians raided Wuyang, Shenji sent envoys to explain fortune and disaster; the barbarians were greatly pleased and returned all they had plundered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Leshan tribes raided Wuyang, Shenji sent envoys to explain the consequences of their actions; the tribes were greatly pleased and returned everything they had taken.

sentences.zh: 又莫世堪負險強黠，抄劫邊戶，為疆場患。

translations.literal: Also Mo Shikan relied on dangerous terrain, was strong and cunning, plundered frontier households, and was a scourge on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Shikan, too, held treacherous ground, was bold and cunning, and raided frontier households, becoming a plague on the border.

sentences.zh: 伸己設伏擒捕，皆置於法。

translations.literal: Shenji set an ambush to capture them; all were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji laid an ambush, captured them, and punished them all according to law.

sentences.zh: 遷果州團練使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regimental trainer of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regimental trainer of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 在宜二年，徙桂州，改右武衛大將軍，守本官分司西京，卒。

translations.literal: After two years at Yizhou he was transferred to Guizhou, changed to General of the Right Martial Guard, retained his original office but served in absentia at the Western Capital, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After two years at Yizhou he was transferred to Guizhou, made general of the Right Martial Guard, and retained his title while serving in absentia at the Western Capital, where he died.

sentences.zh: 始，安化蠻叛，區希範應募擊賊。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Anhua barbarians rebelled, Qu Xifan answered the recruitment to strike the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Anhua tribes first rebelled, Qu Xifan answered the call to fight the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊平，希範詣闕，自言其功。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Xifan came to court and spoke of his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, Xifan came to court and claimed credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 朝廷下宜州，伸己謂希範無功妄要賞，遂編管全州。

translations.literal: The court forwarded the matter to Yizhou; Shenji held that Xifan had no merit yet presumptuously sought reward, and had him registered and banished to Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court referred the matter to Yizhou; Shenji judged that Xifan had no merit and was presumptuously seeking reward, and had him registered and banished to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後希範遁歸，謀為亂，欲殺伸己，嶺外騷然，議者皆罪伸己焉。

translations.literal: Later Xifan escaped and returned, plotted rebellion, and wished to kill Shenji; beyond the ranges turmoil arose, and debaters all blamed Shenji.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xifan escaped, returned, plotted rebellion, and sought to kill Shenji; turmoil spread across the Lingnan region, and critics all blamed Shenji.

sentences.zh: 賈昌朝

translations.literal: Jia Changchao
translations.idiomatic: Jia Changchao

sentences.zh: 賈昌朝，字子明，真定獲鹿人。

translations.literal: Jia Changchao, styled Ziming, was a native of Huolu in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Changchao, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Huolu in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 晉史官緯之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Jia Wei, historiographer of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Jia Wei, historiographer of Jin.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，真宗嘗祈穀南郊，昌朝獻頌道左，召試，賜同進士出身，主晉陵簿。

translations.literal: Early in the Tianxi era, when Emperor Zhenzong performed the southern-suburb grain-prayer sacrifice, Changchao presented a eulogy by the roadside; summoned for examination, he was granted jinshi status with other passers and served as registrar of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxi era, when Emperor Zhenzong performed the southern-suburb grain-prayer rite, Changchao presented a eulogy by the roadside. Summoned for examination, he was granted jinshi standing and appointed registrar of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 賜對便殿，除國子監說書。

translations.literal: Granted audience in the Convenient Hall, he was appointed lecturer at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Granted audience in the Convenient Hall, he was appointed lecturer at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 孫奭判監，獨稱昌朝講說有師法。

translations.literal: Sun Shi was director of the directorate and alone praised Changchao's lectures as having a master's method.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shi, director of the directorate, alone praised Changchao's lectures as truly masterful.

sentences.zh: 他日書路隨、韋處厚傳示昌朝曰：“君當以經術進，如二公。”

translations.literal: Another day he wrote out the biographies of Lu Sui and Wei Chuhou to show Changchao, saying: "You should advance through the classics, like these two gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: On another day he copied out the biographies of Lu Sui and Wei Chuhou and showed them to Changchao, saying, "You should rise through classical learning, as these two men did."

sentences.zh: 為潁川郡王院伴讀。

translations.literal: He became companion reader for the Prince of Yingchuan's household.
translations.idiomatic: He became companion reader for the Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 再遷殿中丞，曆知宜興、東明縣。

translations.literal: Twice promoted to Palace Administration Director, he served in succession as magistrate of Yixing and Dongming counties.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted twice to palace administration director, he served in turn as magistrate of Yixing and Dongming.

sentences.zh: 奭侍讀禁中，以老辭，薦昌朝自代，召試中書，尋復國子監說書。

translations.literal: Shi served as reader-in-waiting in the forbidden precincts; citing old age he resigned and recommended Changchao to replace him. Summoned for examination at the Secretariat, he soon resumed as lecturer at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi served as reader-in-waiting in the palace, he resigned on account of age and recommended Changchao as his successor. Summoned for examination at the Secretariat, Changchao soon resumed as lecturer at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 上言：“禮，母之諱不出於宮。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "By ritual, taboo on the mother's name does not extend outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "By ritual, taboo on one's mother's name does not extend beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 今章獻太后易月製除，猶諱父名，非尊宗廟也。”

translations.literal: Now Empress Dowager Zhangxian, though the mourning period had passed, still tabooed her father's name—this does not honor the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Empress Dowager Zhangxian, though her mourning period had ended, still observed taboo on her father's name. That does not honor the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict adopting his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，置崇政殿說書，以授昌朝。

translations.literal: In the Jingyou era the Chongzheng Hall lectureship was established and conferred on Changchao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyou era the Chongzheng Hall lectureship was created and given to Changchao.

sentences.zh: 誦說明白，帝多所質問，昌朝請記錄以進，賜名《邇英延義記注》，加直集賢院。

translations.literal: His lecturing was clear; the emperor often questioned him at length. Changchao requested that records be kept and submitted; it was given the title Record and Annotation of Erecting Excellence and Extending Righteousness, and he was added as direct academician of the Assembled Worthies Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His lectures were lucid, and the emperor questioned him often. Changchao asked that their exchanges be recorded and submitted; the work was titled Record and Annotation of Erecting Excellence and Extending Righteousness, and he was made direct academician of the Assembled Worthies Hall.

sentences.zh: 太平興國寺災，是夕，大雨震雷。

translations.literal: When Taiping Xingguo Temple burned, that night heavy rain and thunder shook the sky.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping Xingguo Temple burned, that same night came torrential rain and thunder.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議修復，昌朝上言：“《易·震》之象曰：‘洊雷震，君子以恐懼修省。

translations.literal: The court debated restoration; Changchao memorialized: "The image of Zhen in the Book of Changes says: 'Repeated thunder—through fear the noble man examines and reforms himself.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated rebuilding it. Changchao memorialized, "The Zhen hexagram in the Book of Changes says, 'Repeated thunder—the noble man, in fear and awe, examines himself and reforms.

sentences.zh: ’近年寺觀屢災，此殆天示警告，可勿繕治，以示畏天愛人之意。”

translations.literal: ' In recent years temples and monasteries have repeatedly burned—this is probably Heaven showing a warning. Repairs may be omitted, to display the intent to fear Heaven and cherish the people."
translations.idiomatic: ' Temples and monasteries have burned repeatedly in recent years—this is surely Heaven's warning. We should refrain from rebuilding, to show that we fear Heaven and cherish the people.

sentences.zh: 西域僧獻佛骨、銅像，昌朝請加賜遣還，毋以所獻示中外。

translations.literal: A western-region monk presented Buddha relics and a bronze image; Changchao requested additional gifts and their return, and that the offerings not be displayed within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: When a western monk presented Buddha relics and a bronze image, Changchao asked that he be richly rewarded and sent home, and that the gifts not be displayed at court or abroad.

sentences.zh: 悉行其言。

translations.literal: All his proposals were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All his recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 天章閣置侍講，亦首命昌朝。

translations.literal: When the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation established readers-in-waiting, Changchao was again first appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When readers-in-waiting were established at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation, Changchao was again the first appointed.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書禮部郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 劉平為元昊所執，邊吏誣平降賊，議收其家。

translations.literal: Liu Ping was captured by Yuanhao; frontier officials falsely charged that Ping had surrendered to the enemy, and debaters wished to confiscate his family property.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping was captured by Yuanhao; frontier officials falsely accused him of surrendering to the enemy, and some argued for confiscating his family's property.

sentences.zh: 昌朝曰：“漢族殺李陵，陵不得歸，而漢悔之。

translations.literal: Changchao said: "The Han executed Li Ling's clan; Ling could not return, and the Han regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao said, "The Han executed Li Ling's clan; Li Ling could not return, and the Han came to regret it.

sentences.zh: 先帝厚撫王繼忠家，終得繼忠用。

translations.literal: The late emperor generously provided for Wang Jizhong's family and in the end was able to employ Jizhong.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor treated Wang Jizhong's family generously and in the end was able to use Jizhong again.

sentences.zh: 平事未可知，使收其族，雖平在，亦不得還矣。”

translations.literal: Ping's situation is not yet known; if his clan is confiscated, even if Ping survives he will not be able to return."
translations.idiomatic: Ping's fate is still unknown. If we seize his family, even should he survive he will never be able to come home."

sentences.zh: 乃得不收。

translations.literal: Thus the family was not confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The family was spared confiscation.

sentences.zh: 擢知制誥、權判吏部流內銓兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was promoted to draft proclamations, acting director of the Ministry of Personnel's flowing-within selection board concurrently reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of proclamations, acting director of the Ministry of Personnel's flowing-within selection board, and reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 初，銓法，縣令奉錢滿萬二千，乃舉令。

translations.literal: Initially, under selection law, a county magistrate's salary had to reach twelve thousand before he could be promoted as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Under the selection rules, a county magistrate's salary had to reach twelve thousand before he could be promoted to a magistracy.

sentences.zh: 昌朝曰：“法如此，則小縣終不得善令。”

translations.literal: Changchao said: "If the law is thus, small counties will never obtain good magistrates."
translations.idiomatic: Changchao said, "If the law stands thus, small counties will never get capable magistrates."

sentences.zh: 請概舉令，而與之奉如大縣。”

translations.literal: He requested universal promotion of magistrates and granting them salaries like those of large counties.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that magistrates be promoted broadly and paid at the same rate as those in large counties.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣直學士、權知開封府，遷右諫議大夫、權御史中丞兼判國子監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, acting prefect of Kaifeng; he was transferred to Right Remonstration Grandee, acting Censor-in-Chief concurrently supervising the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and acting prefect of Kaifeng, then to right remonstration grandee, acting censor-in-chief, and supervisor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 議者欲以金繒啖契丹使攻元昊，昌朝曰：“契丹許我有功，則責報無窮矣。”

translations.literal: Debaters wished to use gold and silk to bribe the Khitan into attacking Yuanhao; Changchao said: "If the Khitan agree to act for our benefit, then demands for reward will be endless."
translations.idiomatic: Some argued for bribing the Khitan with gold and silk to attack Yuanhao. Changchao said, "If the Khitan agree to help us, their demands for reward will never end."

sentences.zh: 力止之。

translations.literal: He forcefully stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: He forcefully blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 乃上言曰：“太祖初有天下，監唐末五代方鎮武臣、土兵牙校之盛，盡收其威權，當時以為萬世之利。

translations.literal: Then he memorialized: "When Taizu first possessed the empire, seeing the strength of Tang-and-Five-Dynasties frontier military commissioners, territorial soldiers, and army clerks, he gathered all their authority to himself—at the time this was regarded as a benefit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized, "When Taizu first won the empire, he saw how powerful the frontier military commissioners, local troops, and army clerks of the late Tang and Five Dynasties had become, and he gathered all their authority to the throne. At the time this was thought a blessing for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 及太宗時，將帥率多舊人，猶能仗威靈，稟成算，出師禦寇，所向有功。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Taizong, generals and commanders were for the most part old associates, yet still able to rely on imperial authority, receive completed plans, lead armies out to repel invaders, and achieve merit wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong, most commanders were still veterans of the founding generation. Drawing on imperial authority and plans laid down for them, they marched out to repel enemies and won victories wherever they fought.

sentences.zh: 近歲恩幸子弟，飾廚傳，釣名譽，多非勳勞，坐取武爵，折衝攻守，彼何自而知哉？

translations.literal: In recent years, sons of favored courtiers, embellishing relay-station hospitality, fishing for reputation, mostly without meritorious service, merely by sitting obtain military ranks—how would they themselves know about breaking the enemy's charge, attacking, and defending?
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, sons of imperial favorites have lavished hospitality at relay stations and courted fame. Having done little to earn merit, they have nonetheless sat their way into military ranks. What could such men know of breaking enemy charges, of assault and defense?

sentences.zh: 然邊鄙無事，尚得自容。

translations.literal: Yet when the frontier was peaceful, they could still manage to save face.
translations.idiomatic: So long as the borders were quiet, they could still get by.

sentences.zh: 自西羌之叛，士不練習，將不得人，以屢易之將馭不練之士，故戰則必敗。

translations.literal: Since the rebellion of the Western Qiang, soldiers were not trained, good commanders were not obtained, and frequently changed generals drove untrained troops—therefore whenever they fought they were certain to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Western Qiang rose in revolt, troops have gone untrained and the wrong men have been put in command. Generals rotated in and out have led raw soldiers into battle—and defeat has followed every time.

sentences.zh: 此削方鎮太過之弊也。

translations.literal: This is the harm of having curtailed the regional commands too far.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the cost of having stripped the frontier commands of too much power.

sentences.zh: 況親舊、恩幸，出即為將，素不知兵，一旦付以千萬人之命，是驅之死地矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, relatives, old associates, and favored ones—upon leaving court they immediately become generals, never having known military affairs; once entrusted with the lives of millions, this is driving them to their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, relatives, old cronies, and imperial favorites are made generals the moment they leave court, though they know nothing of war. To hand them command over millions of lives is to drive those lives—and their own—to ruin.

sentences.zh: 此用親舊、恩幸之弊也。

translations.literal: This is the harm of employing relatives, old associates, and favored ones.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the harm of filling commands with kin, cronies, and favorites.

sentences.zh: 今楊崇勳、李昭亮尚任邊鄙，望速選士代之。

translations.literal: Now Yang Chongxun and Li Zhaoliang still hold frontier posts; I hope capable men may quickly be selected to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongxun and Li Zhaoliang still hold frontier commands today. I urge that qualified replacements be chosen at once.

sentences.zh: 方鎮守臣無數更易，刺史以上，宜慎所授，以待有功。

translations.literal: Frontier garrison commanders are changed without number; for prefects and above, appointments should be made with care, waiting until they have merit.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrison commanders are rotated endlessly. Appointments from prefect upward should be made carefully and reserved for men who have proven themselves.

sentences.zh: 此救弊之一端也。”

translations.literal: This is one measure to remedy the abuses.
translations.idiomatic: This would be one step toward setting things right.

sentences.zh: 又上備邊六事：

translations.literal: He again submitted the Six Measures for Border Defense:
translations.idiomatic: He further submitted six proposals for strengthening the frontier:

sentences.zh: 其一曰馭將帥。

translations.literal: The first is controlling generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: First: governing commanders.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王，以恩威馭將帥，賞罰馭士卒，用命則軍政行而戰功集。

translations.literal: From antiquity, emperors and kings controlled generals and commanders through kindness and severity, controlled troops through rewards and punishments—when they obeyed, military administration proceeded and battle achievements accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, sovereigns have governed their commanders with a blend of grace and authority, and governed soldiers through reward and punishment. When men obey, military discipline holds and victories follow.

sentences.zh: 太祖脫裘帽賜王全斌曰：“今日居此幄，尚寒不可禦，況伐蜀將士乎？”

translations.literal: Taizu removed his fur coat and cap and bestowed them on Wang Quanbin, saying: "Today, dwelling in this tent, it is still so cold one cannot withstand it—how much more so the officers and soldiers campaigning against Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu took off his fur coat and cap and gave them to Wang Quanbin, saying, "Even here in this tent I can barely keep warm—what must it be like for the men marching against Shu?"

sentences.zh: 此馭之以恩也。

translations.literal: This is controlling them through kindness.
translations.idiomatic: That was governing through kindness.

sentences.zh: 曹彬、李漢瓊討江南，太祖召彬至前，立漢瓊等於後，授以劍曰：“副將以下，不用命者得專戮之。”

translations.literal: When Cao Bin and Li Hanqiong campaigned against Jiangnan, Taizu summoned Bin to the front, placed Hanqiong and the others behind, and handed them a sword, saying: "For deputy commanders and below, those who disobey may be executed on your sole authority."
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin and Li Hanqiong marched against Jiangnan, Taizu called Bin forward, placed Hanqiong and the others behind him, and presented a sword, saying, "Any deputy commander or officer who disobeys may be put to death at your sole discretion."

sentences.zh: 漢瓊等股栗而退，此馭之以威也。

translations.literal: Hanqiong and the others, legs trembling, withdrew—this is controlling through severity.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiong and the others withdrew with trembling legs. That was governing through fear.

sentences.zh: 太祖雖削武臣之權，然一時賞罰及用財集事，皆聽其專，有功則賞，有敗則誅。

translations.literal: Although Taizu curtailed the power of military officers, for a time rewards and punishments and the use of funds to accomplish tasks were all left to their exclusive discretion—merit was rewarded, failure was punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Though Taizu had limited the power of military men, he still let them decide rewards, punishments, and spending on the spot. Success was rewarded; failure meant death.

sentences.zh: 今每命將帥，必先疑貳，非近幸不信，非姻舊不委。

translations.literal: Now, whenever generals and commanders are appointed, suspicion comes first—if not a close favorite, they are not trusted; if not a kinsman or old associate, they are not entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Today, every time a commander is appointed, the court begins with distrust. Only imperial favorites are trusted; only kin and old allies receive real authority.

sentences.zh: 今陝西四路，總管而下，鈐轄、都監、巡檢之屬，悉參軍政，謀之未成，事已先漏，甲可乙否，上行下戾，主將不專號令，故動則必敗。

translations.literal: Now in the four circuits of Shaanxi, from circuit commander down, controllers, chief supervisors, inspectors, and the like all participate in military administration—before plans are finished, affairs are already leaked; one approves what another rejects, the upper go one way and the lower another, the chief commander does not monopolize orders, therefore whenever they act they are certain to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaanxi's four frontier circuits today, everyone from the circuit commander down—deputy commanders, supervisors, inspectors—has a hand in military affairs. Plans leak before they are settled; one officer approves what another rejects; orders conflict between top and bottom. With no single voice in command, defeat follows every campaign.

sentences.zh: 請自今命將，去疑貳，推恩惠，務責以大效，得一切便宜從事。

translations.literal: I request that from now on, when appointing generals, remove suspicion, extend kindness and grace, charge them to achieve great results, and allow them full discretionary authority to act as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when appointing commanders, I urge the court to abandon suspicion, extend trust and favor, hold them accountable for results, and grant full authority to act as need requires.

sentences.zh: 偏裨有不聽令者，以軍法論，此馭將之道也。

translations.literal: When subordinate officers do not obey orders, they should be dealt with by military law—this is the way to control generals.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates who disobey should answer to military law. That is how commanders should be governed.

sentences.zh: 其二曰復土兵。

translations.literal: The second is restoring local militia.
translations.idiomatic: Second: restoring local militia.

sentences.zh: 今河北河東強壯、陝西弓箭手之類，土兵遺法也。

translations.literal: Now the stalwart militia of Hebei and Hedong, Shaanxi archers, and the like are vestiges of the local militia system.
translations.idiomatic: The stalwart militia of Hebei and Hedong, the archers of Shaanxi—these are remnants of the old local militia system.

sentences.zh: 河北鄉兵，其廢已久，陝西土兵，數為賊破，存者無幾。

translations.literal: Hebei village militia have long since been abolished; Shaanxi local militia have repeatedly been broken by bandits, and few survivors remain.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei's village militia were scrapped long ago. Shaanxi's local militia have been shattered again and again by rebels; scarcely any remain.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂河北、河東強壯，已召近臣詳定法製，每鄉為軍。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that for the stalwart militia of Hebei and Hedong, near ministers have already been summoned to work out regulations in detail, organizing each village as a unit.
translations.idiomatic: For the stalwart militia of Hebei and Hedong, I believe the court has already summoned senior officials to draw up regulations, organizing each village as a military unit.

sentences.zh: 其材能絕類者，籍其姓名遞補之。

translations.literal: Those whose talent and ability surpass their peers should have their names registered for successive promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Men of exceptional ability should be listed by name and promoted in turn.

sentences.zh: 陝西蕃落弓箭手，貪召募錢物，利月入糧奉，多就黥涅為營兵。

translations.literal: Shaanxi tribal archers, coveting recruitment money and goods, finding advantage in monthly grain stipends, mostly submit to tattooing and become camp soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal archers in Shaanxi, drawn by enlistment bonuses and monthly rations, mostly accept tattooing and enlist as regular camp soldiers instead.

sentences.zh: 宜優復田疇，使力耕死戰，世為邊用，可以減屯戍、省供饋矣。

translations.literal: They should be given preferential restoration of fields, made to work the land strenuously and fight to the death, serving the frontier generation after generation—thus garrison troops can be reduced and supplies saved.
translations.idiomatic: They should be granted favorable access to farmland, encouraged to farm hard and fight hard, and passed down from generation to generation as frontier auxiliaries. This would cut garrison numbers and save supply costs.

sentences.zh: 內地州縣，增置弓手，如鄉軍之法而閱試之。

translations.literal: In interior prefectures and counties, increase archers, reviewing and testing them by the method of village armies.
translations.idiomatic: In interior prefectures and counties, additional archers should be enrolled and drilled according to the village-army model.

sentences.zh: 其三曰訓營卒。

translations.literal: The third is training camp soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Third: training regular soldiers.

sentences.zh: 太祖朝，令諸軍毋得食肉衣帛，營舍有粥酒肴則逐去，士卒有服繒彩者笞責之。

translations.literal: In Taizu's reign, he ordered all armies not to eat meat or wear silk; if camp quarters had congee, wine, or meat dishes they were driven away; soldiers wearing colored silk were flogged and reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu, armies were forbidden meat and silk clothing. Any camp found serving rich food or wine had it cleared away; soldiers caught in colored silks were whipped.

sentences.zh: 異時被鎧甲、冒霜露，戰勝攻取，皆此曹也。

translations.literal: In former times, those who donned armor, braved frost and dew, won battles and took by assault—it was all these men.
translations.idiomatic: The men who once donned armor, endured frost and cold, and won their battles were exactly these disciplined troops.

sentences.zh: 今營卒驕惰，臨敵無勇。

translations.literal: Now camp soldiers are arrogant and lazy; facing the enemy they have no courage.
translations.idiomatic: Today's soldiers are spoiled and slack; they lack courage when the enemy appears.

sentences.zh: 舊例三年轉員，謂之落權正授，雖未能易此製，即不必一例使為總管、鈐轄，擇有才勇可任將帥者授之。

translations.literal: The old rule is transfer of personnel every three years, called removal from acting appointment to formal appointment; although this system cannot be changed, it is not necessary to uniformly make them all circuit commanders and controllers—select those with talent and courage who can serve as generals and commanders and appoint them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, soldiers rotate every three years from acting to formal rank—a system we need not abolish. But not every man need be made a circuit commander or deputy. Choose those with talent and courage fit for command.

sentences.zh: 況今之兵仗製造，殊不適用。

translations.literal: Moreover, the manufacture of weapons today is quite unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the weapons produced today are quite unsuited to actual use.

sentences.zh: 宜按八陣、五兵之法，以時教習。

translations.literal: They should follow the methods of the Eight Formations and the Five Weapons, drilling them according to season.
translations.idiomatic: Troops should be drilled seasonally according to the Eight Formations and the Five Weapons.

sentences.zh: 使啟殿有次序、左右有形勢，前卻相附，上下相援，令之曰：“失一隊長，則斬一隊。”

translations.literal: Cause them to advance and deploy in order, left and right with tactical advantage, advancing and retreating in mutual support, upper and lower in mutual aid—command them, saying: "Lose one squad leader, and the whole squad is executed."
translations.idiomatic: Train them to advance and deploy in order, with solid formations on left and right, mutual support in advance and retreat, and coordination between front and rear. Issue this order: "Lose one squad leader, and the entire squad dies."

sentences.zh: 何慮眾不為用乎？

translations.literal: Why worry that the multitude will not be of use?
translations.idiomatic: Why then worry that the men will not fight?

sentences.zh: 其四曰制遠人。

translations.literal: The fourth is controlling distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: managing distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 今四夷蕩然與中國通，在北則臣契丹，其西則臣元昊，二國合從，有掎角中國之勢。

translations.literal: Now the four barbarians are entirely open in communication with China; in the north they submit to the Khitan, in the west they submit to Yuan Hao—the two states unite, possessing the momentum of pincering China.
translations.idiomatic: Today the border peoples deal freely with the Middle Kingdom. To the north they look to the Khitan; to the west they look to Yuan Hao. Those two powers have joined forces and now threaten to pinch China between them.

sentences.zh: 借使以歲幣羈縻之，臣恐不可勝算。

translations.literal: Even if we used annual tribute to keep them tethered, your subject fears the cost cannot be calculated.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we tried to buy their loyalty with annual tribute, I fear the cost would be beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 古之備邊，西有金城、上郡，北則雲中、雁門。

translations.literal: In antiquity, defending the frontier, in the west were Jincheng and Shangjun; in the north, Yunzhong and Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, frontier defense relied on strongholds: Jincheng and Shangjun in the west, Yunzhong and Yanmen in the north.

sentences.zh: 今自滄之秦，綿亙數千里，無山河之阻，獨恃州縣鎮戍爾。

translations.literal: Now from Cangzhou to Qinzhou, stretching thousands of li, there are no river-and-mountain barriers—relying solely on prefecture, county, and garrison strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: Today from Cangzhou to Qinzhou the frontier runs thousands of li without river or mountain barriers to shield it—we depend on nothing but prefectural garrisons.

sentences.zh: 歲所供贍，又不下數千萬，一穀不熟，或至狼狽。

translations.literal: Yearly provisions supplied amount to no less than tens of millions; one poor harvest and we may fall into dire straits.
translations.idiomatic: Annual frontier supplies cost tens of millions of cash. One failed harvest can leave the whole system in crisis.

sentences.zh: 契丹近歲兼用燕人治國，建官一同中夏。

translations.literal: The Khitan in recent years have combined use of Yan people to govern the state, establishing offices identical to the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the Khitan have put men from Yan to work governing their realm, building an administrative system modeled on China's own.

sentences.zh: 元昊據河南列郡而行賞罰，此中國患也。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao holds the southern river prefectures and enforces rewards and punishments—this is China's worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao holds the Henan prefectures and enforces his own law there—that is China's grave concern.

sentences.zh: 宜度西方諸國如沙州、唃廝、明珠、滅臧之族，近北如黑水女真、高麗、新羅之屬，舊通中國，募人往使，誘之使歸我，則勢分而釁生，體解而瓦裂矣。

translations.literal: We should consider western states such as Shazhou, Gusiluo, Mingzhu, and Miezang tribes, and those near the north like the Heishui Jurchen, Goryeo, and Silla—all formerly in communication with China—send envoys to entice them to return to us; then their strength would be divided and discord would arise, the body would disintegrate and shatter like tiles.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the western realms—Shazhou, Gusiluo, Mingzhu, Miezang—and northern peoples such as the Heishui Jurchen, Goryeo, and Silla, all once linked to China. Send envoys to win them back. Their alliance would split, quarrels would arise, and the enemy would break apart like shattered tile.

sentences.zh: 其五曰綏蕃部。

translations.literal: The fifth is pacifying tribal departments.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: securing tribal allies.

sentences.zh: 屬戶者，邊垂之屏翰也。

translations.literal: Dependent households are the protective screen of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Dependent households are the frontier's shield.

sentences.zh: 延有金明，府有豐州，皆戎人內附之地。

translations.literal: Yanzhou has Jinming, Fuzhou has Fengzhou—all places where barbarians submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming in Yanzhou, Fengzhou in Fuzhou—these are lands where tribal peoples came over to the court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恩威不立，強敵迫之，塞上諸州，藐焉孤壘，蕃部既壞，土兵亦衰，破敵之日，未可期也。

translations.literal: When the court's kindness and severity are not established, strong enemies press them, the frontier prefectures are like isolated forts held in contempt; once tribal departments are ruined, local militia also decline—the day of defeating the enemy cannot yet be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: When the court shows neither firm kindness nor authority, powerful enemies press in, and frontier prefectures stand as lonely, neglected outposts. Once tribal allies collapse, local militia weaken too—and victory becomes a distant hope.

sentences.zh: 臣請陝西緣邊諸路，守臣皆帶“安撫蕃部”之名，擇其族大有勞者為酋帥，如河東折氏之比，庶可為吾藩籬之固也。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that on all Shaanxi frontier circuits, defending officials all bear the title "Pacifier of Tribal Departments," selecting those of the tribe with great merit as chieftains, like the Zhe clan of Hedong—then perhaps they can serve as the solid fence of our defense.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that frontier officials throughout Shaanxi bear the title "Pacifier of Tribal Allies," with tribal leaders of proven merit appointed as chieftains—following the example of the Zhe clan in Hedong—so they may serve as a firm bulwark for the realm.

sentences.zh: 其六曰謹覘候。

translations.literal: The sixth is careful reconnaissance.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: vigilant scouting.

sentences.zh: 古者守封疆，出師旅，居則有行人之覘國，戰則有前茅之慮無，其謹如此。

translations.literal: In antiquity, guarding borders and dispatching armies—in peacetime there were envoys to observe states, in war there were vanguard scouts to guard against the unexpected—such was their caution.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, whether guarding borders or marching to war, peacetime relied on envoys to watch foreign states and wartime on vanguard scouts to guard against surprise—such was their vigilance.

sentences.zh: 太祖命李漢超鎮關南，馬仁瑀守瀛州，韓令坤鎮常山，賀惟忠守易州，何繼筠領棣州，郭進控山西，武守琪戍晉陽，李謙溥守隰州，董遵誨屯環州，王彥升守原州，馮繼業鎮靈武。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Li Hanchao to garrison Guannan, Ma Renyu to defend Yingzhou, Han Lingkun to garrison Changshan, He Weizhong to defend Yizhou, He Jiyun to command Dizhou, Guo Jin to control Shanxi, Wu Shouqi to garrison Jinyang, Li Qianbo to defend Xizhou, Dong Zunhui to encamp at Huanzhou, Wang Yansheng to defend Yuanzhou, and Feng Jiye to garrison Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu posted Li Hanchao at Guannan, Ma Renyu at Yingzhou, Han Lingkun at Changshan, He Weizhong at Yizhou, He Jiyun at Dizhou, Guo Jin over Shanxi, Wu Shouqi at Jinyang, Li Qianbo at Xizhou, Dong Zunhui at Huanzhou, Wang Yansheng at Yuanzhou, and Feng Jiye at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 筦榷之利，悉輸之軍中，聽其貿易，而免其征稅。

translations.literal: Monopoly profits were all delivered to the armies, allowing them to trade and exempting them from taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly revenues went entirely to the frontier armies, which were free to trade without paying taxes.

sentences.zh: 邊臣富於財，得以為間諜，羌夷情狀，無不預知。

translations.literal: Frontier officials were rich in funds, and able to employ spies—the conditions of Qiang and barbarians were all foreknown.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with funds, frontier commanders could run spies and learn everything about tribal movements before events unfolded.

sentences.zh: 二十年間，無外顧之憂。

translations.literal: For twenty years, there was no worry of threats from outside.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years the court need not fear attack from beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 今日西鄙任邊事者，敵之情狀與山川、道路險易之勢，絕不通曉。

translations.literal: Today those in the western frontier charged with border affairs are utterly ignorant of enemy conditions and the advantages and difficulties of mountains, rivers, and roads.
translations.idiomatic: Today the men who run the western frontier know almost nothing of the enemy—or of the terrain and roads they must traverse.

sentences.zh: 使蹈不測之淵，入萬死之地，肝腦塗地，狼狽相藉，何以破敵制勝耶？

translations.literal: Sending them to tread unfathomable depths, enter lands of ten thousand deaths, brains and blood smeared on the ground, dire straits piled upon one another—how can they break the enemy and achieve victory?
translations.idiomatic: How can men who stumble into unknown depths and lands where death waits at every step—where brains and blood soak the ground and bodies fall in heaps—hope to defeat the enemy and win?

sentences.zh: 願監藝祖任將帥之制，邊城財用悉以委之。

translations.literal: I wish to follow Founder Taizu's system of appointing generals and commanders, entrusting all frontier city funds and resources to them entirely.
translations.idiomatic: I urge the court to restore Emperor Taizu's practice: give frontier commanders full control over local finances.

sentences.zh: 募敢勇之士為爪牙，臨陣自衛，無殺將之辱；

translations.literal: Recruit bold and brave men as claws and fangs; in battle they protect themselves—no disgrace of generals being killed.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit bold warriors as personal guards so commanders can defend themselves in battle and avoid the shame of being cut down.

sentences.zh: 募死力為覘候，而望敵知來，無陷兵之恥。

translations.literal: Recruit men willing to die as scouts, so that looking toward the enemy they know what comes—no shame of troops being trapped.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit men willing to die as scouts, so the enemy's approach is never a surprise and troops are never trapped in ambush.

sentences.zh: 書奏，多施行之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; much of it was put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and much of it was adopted.

sentences.zh: 昌朝請度經費，罷不急。

translations.literal: Changchao requested measuring expenditures and abolishing what was not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao proposed reviewing expenditures and cutting nonessential spending.

sentences.zh: 詔與三司合議，歲所省緡錢百萬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered joint deliberation with the Three Departments; yearly savings amounted to one million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him to confer with the fiscal ministry; they agreed on annual savings of one million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 又言：“朝臣七十，筋力衰者，宜依典故致仕，有功狀可留者勿拘。”

translations.literal: He further said: "Court officials at seventy whose strength has declined should retire according to precedent; those with records of merit who may be retained should not be constrained."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "Officials of seventy whose strength has waned should retire as precedent dictates; those with proven records of service may remain at their posts."

sentences.zh: 因疏耄昏不任事者八人，令致仕。

translations.literal: Accordingly he listed eight who were aged, muddled, and unable to handle affairs, ordering their retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He then named eight officials too aged and feeble to serve and had them retired.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingli, he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 3 he was made Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 上言：“用兵以來，天下民力頗困。

translations.literal: He submitted: "Since warfare began, the people's strength throughout the realm is quite strained."
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Since the war began, the people's resources have been severely strained."

sentences.zh: 請詔諸路轉運使，毋得承例折變科率，須科折者，悉聽奏裁。

translations.literal: I request an edict to transport commissioners of all circuits that they must not follow precedent in commutation and forced extraction; wherever commutation is required, all must await imperial decision by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that transport commissioners be forbidden to impose forced commutation levies by precedent; wherever commutation is needed, they must seek imperial approval first.

sentences.zh: 雖奉旨及三司文移，於民不便者，亦以上聞。”

translations.literal: Even when following edicts and documents from the Three Departments, if something is inconvenient for the people, it should also be reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Even orders from the throne or the fiscal ministry should be reported upward if they harm the people.

sentences.zh: 以工部侍郎充樞密使，尋拜同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士，仍兼樞密使。

translations.literal: As Vice Minister of Works he served as Commissioner of Military Affairs; soon he was appointed Co-Grand Councillor of the Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi, Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies, still concurrently Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Minister of Works he became Commissioner of Military Affairs; soon he was made Grand Councillor, Grand Academician of the Hall for Collecting Worthies, while retaining his post at Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 居兩月，拜昭文館大學士，監修國史。

translations.literal: After two months, he was appointed Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and Supervisor of Compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later he was made Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 元昊歸石元孫，議賜死。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao returned Shi Yuansun; deliberation was held on sentencing him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao returned the captive Shi Yuansun, the court debated sentencing him to death.

sentences.zh: 昌朝獨曰：“自古將帥被執，歸者多不死。”

translations.literal: Changchao alone said: "From antiquity, when generals and commanders were captured, those who returned mostly were not executed."
translations.idiomatic: Changchao alone argued: "Throughout history, captured generals who were returned were rarely put to death."

sentences.zh: 元孫由是得免。

translations.literal: Yuansun thereby obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansun was spared as a result.

sentences.zh: 詔有司議升祔奉慈廟三后，有司論不一。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate on elevating the three empresses to attendant enshrinement at Fengci Temple; the offices' opinions were not unified.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered officials to debate enshrining the three empresses alongside the emperor at Fengci Temple, but they could not agree.

sentences.zh: 昌朝曰：“章獻母儀天下，章懿誕育聖躬，宜如詳符升祔元德皇后故事。

translations.literal: Changchao said: "Empress Zhangxian was motherly model to the realm, Empress Zhangyi bore the sacred person—the manner should follow the Xiangfu precedent of elevating Empress Yuande to attendant enshrinement."
translations.idiomatic: Changchao argued: "Empress Zhangxian embodied maternal virtue for the realm; Empress Zhangyi bore the emperor. They should be enshrined as Empress Yuande was at Xiangfu."

sentences.zh: 章惠於陛下有慈保之恩，當別享奉慈廟如故。”

translations.literal: Empress Zhanghui had kindness and nurturing grace toward Your Majesty; she should separately receive offering at Fengci Temple as before.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhanghui nursed and cared for Your Majesty; she should continue to receive separate rites at Fengci Temple.

sentences.zh: 乃奉二后神主，升祔真宗廟。

translations.literal: Thereupon the spirit tablets of the two empresses were offered and elevated to attendant enshrinement at Emperor Zhenzong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets of the two empresses were then installed in Emperor Zhenzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 密詔遷中外官一等，優賜諸軍，昌朝與同列力疏，乃止。

translations.literal: A secret edict ordered promoting inner and outer officials one rank and granting generous gifts to all armies; Changchao and colleagues vigorously remonstrated, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict ordered a one-rank promotion for all officials and generous bonuses for the armies. Changchao and his colleagues protested forcefully, and the order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 又詔遷二府官，益固辭。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered promoting the Two Departments' officials; he all the more firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When another edict proposed promoting officials of the Two Departments, he refused even more firmly.

sentences.zh: 元昊既款附，請宰相罷兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Once Yuan Hao had sworn allegiance, he requested that grand councillors cease concurrently holding the Military Affairs commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao submitted, he asked that grand councillors no longer hold concurrent posts as Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，日食。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the reign, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 帝謂昌朝等曰：“謫見於天，願歸罪朕躬。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Changchao and others: "The reproach appears in Heaven; I wish to assign guilt to my own person."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Changchao and the others: "Heaven shows its reproach; let the blame fall on me alone."

sentences.zh: 卿宜究民疾苦，思所以利安之。”

translations.literal: You, sirs, should thoroughly investigate the people's hardships and afflictions, and consider means to benefit and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: You must uncover the people's suffering and find ways to ease and restore them.

sentences.zh: 昌朝對曰：“陛下此言，足以弭天變，臣敢不夙夜孜孜以奉陛下。”

translations.literal: Changchao replied: "Your Majesty's words are sufficient to quell Heaven's transformations; how dare your subject not from early morn to late night diligently serve Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Changchao replied: "Your words alone can appease Heaven's wrath. How could I fail to serve you tirelessly, day and night?"

sentences.zh: 帝又曰：“人主懼天而修德，猶人臣畏法而自新也。”

translations.literal: The Emperor again said: "A ruler who fears Heaven and cultivates virtue is like a minister who fears the law and renews himself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added: "When a ruler fears Heaven and reforms his conduct, it is like a subject who respects the law and mends his ways."

sentences.zh: 昌朝因頓首謝。

translations.literal: Changchao thereupon prostrated himself and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao bowed low in acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 明年春，旱，帝避正寢，減膳。

translations.literal: The next spring, there was drought; the Emperor avoided the main palace chamber and reduced his meals.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring drought struck. The emperor moved out of the main palace quarters and cut back his table.

sentences.zh: 昌朝引漢災異冊免三公故事，上表乞罷。

translations.literal: Changchao cited the Han precedent of dismissing the Three Excellencies due to calamities and portents, and submitted a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the Han precedent of dismissing the Three Excellencies after disasters, Changchao submitted a memorial asking to be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 參知政事吳育數與昌朝爭議上前，論者多不直昌朝。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Wu Yu often debated with Changchao before the throne; most commentators did not side with Changchao.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Wu Yu often clashed with Changchao before the emperor, and public opinion mostly sided against Changchao.

sentences.zh: 有向綬者知永靜軍，疑通判譖己，誣以事，迫令自殺。

translations.literal: There was Xiang Shou, who governed Yongjing Army; suspecting the vice prefect slandered him, he falsely charged him with an offense and forced him to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Shou, military governor of Yongjing, suspected his vice prefect of slandering him. He fabricated charges and drove the man to suicide.

sentences.zh: 高若訥知審刑院，附昌朝議，欲從輕坐。

translations.literal: Gao Ruonè, head of the Court of Judicial Review, sided with Changchao's view, wishing to impose a lighter sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruonè of the Court of Judicial Review sided with Changchao and argued for a lighter sentence.

sentences.zh: 吳育力爭，綬卒減死一等。

translations.literal: Wu Yu vigorously contended; Shou ultimately had his death sentence reduced one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu fought the ruling fiercely, and Xiang Shou's death sentence was reduced by one degree.

sentences.zh: 未幾，若訥為御史中丞，言大臣廷爭不肅，故雨不時若，遂罷育，而除昌朝武勝軍節度使、檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事、判大名府兼北京留守司、河北安撫使。

translations.literal: Before long, Ruonè became Censor-in-Chief, saying that grand ministers' court disputes lacked solemnity, hence rain did not come at the proper time; thereupon Wu Yu was dismissed, and Changchao was appointed Military Commissioner of Wusheng Army, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Co-Grand Councillor, Administrator of Daming Prefecture concurrently Director of the Northern Capital Guard, and Hebei Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Ruonè became Censor-in-Chief. He blamed the ministers' unseemly quarrels for the failed rains, and Wu Yu was dismissed. Changchao was made Military Commissioner of Wusheng, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Grand Councillor, Administrator of Daming and director of the northern capital guard, and Hebei Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝賜銀飾肩輿。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed a shoulder carriage inlaid with silver ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him a palanquin adorned with silver fittings.

sentences.zh: 尋以討貝州賊有功，移山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, for merit in suppressing Beizhou bandits, he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, rewarded for crushing the Beizhou rebels, he was made Military Commissioner of the Eastern Mountain South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 楊偕言賊發昌朝部中，不當賞。

translations.literal: Yang Xie said the bandits arose from within Changchao's department and he should not be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xie argued that the rebels had sprung from Changchao's own jurisdiction and that he did not deserve a reward.

sentences.zh: 弗從。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not follow [this].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 契丹聚亡卒勇伉者，號“投來南軍”。

translations.literal: The Khitan gathered fugitive soldiers who were brave and fierce, styled them "The Army That Came Over to the South."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans mustered fugitive soldiers who were bold and fierce into a force they called the "Southern Army of Surrendered Men."

sentences.zh: 邊法，卒亡自歸者死。

translations.literal: Border law: soldiers who deserted and returned on their own were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Under frontier law, any soldier who deserted and then came back on his own was executed.

sentences.zh: 昌朝除其法，歸者輒遷補，於是來者稍眾，因廉知契丹事。

translations.literal: Changchao removed this law; returners were at once transferred and given new posts. Thereupon arrivals gradually grew numerous, and through this he came to know Khitan affairs in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao abolished the law. Every deserter who returned was reassigned and given a new post, and before long the stream of arrivals swelled. He thus gained detailed intelligence on Khitan affairs.

sentences.zh: 契丹遂拒亡卒，黜南軍不用。

translations.literal: The Khitan thereupon refused fugitive soldiers, dismissed the Southern Army and did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans then shut their doors to deserters and disbanded the Southern Army altogether.

sentences.zh: 邊人以地外質，契丹故稍侵邊界。

translations.literal: Border people pawned land outside [the border]; the Khitan therefore gradually encroached on the frontier boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier families had taken to pledging land across the border as collateral, and the Khitans gradually used this to nibble away at the boundary.

sentences.zh: 昌朝為立法，質地而主不時贖，人得贖而有之，歲餘，地悉復。

translations.literal: Changchao made a law: if land was pledged and the owner did not redeem it in time, others could redeem it and possess it. After a little over a year, all the land was fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao drafted a new statute: when pledged land went unredeemed by its owner in the allotted time, anyone else could redeem it and take title. Within a year and more, every acre had been recovered.

sentences.zh: 三司使葉清臣移用河北庫錢，昌朝格詔不與，清臣論列不已，遂出清臣河陽，徙昌朝判鄭州。

translations.literal: Three Departments Commissioner Ye Qingchen diverted Hebei treasury funds; Changchao blocked the edict and would not grant them. Qingchen argued back and forth without cease; thereupon Qingchen was sent out to Heyang, and Changchao was transferred to Administrator of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Qingchen, commissioner of the Three Departments, tried to divert Hebei treasury funds. Changchao blocked the order and refused to release the money. Ye Qingchen kept hammering away in memorials until he was posted to Heyang and Changchao was shifted to administer Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 過闕入覲，留為祥源觀使，拜尚書右僕射、觀文殿大學士、判尚書都省，朝會班中書門下，視其儀物。

translations.literal: Passing the capital to enter audience, he was retained as Commissioner of Xiangyuan Abbey, appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Administrator of the Secretariat Directorate; at court assemblies he ranked with the Chief Secretariat and Chancellery and shared their ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: On his way through the capital for an audience, he was kept at court as commissioner of the Xiangyuan Temple and named Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, and Administrator of the Secretariat Directorate. At court assemblies he took rank alongside the chief ministers and shared their ceremonial insignia.

sentences.zh: 歲中求外，復除山南東道節度使、右僕射、檢校太師兼侍中、判鄭州。

translations.literal: Mid-year he requested an outside posting and was again appointed Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, Right Vice Director, Honorary Grand Preceptor concurrently Palace Attendant, and Administrator of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway through the year he asked for a provincial post and was again named Military Commissioner of the Eastern Mountain South Circuit, Right Vice Director, Honorary Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant, and Administrator of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 固辭僕射、侍中，改同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the posts of Vice Director and Palace Attendant and was changed to Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the posts of Vice Director and Palace Attendant and was made Grand Councillor instead.

sentences.zh: 賜中謝，自昌朝始也。

translations.literal: The bestowing of mid-court thanks began with Changchao.
translations.idiomatic: The custom of thanking the throne from mid-court began with Changchao.

sentences.zh: 母喪去位，服除，判許州。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office; after mourning ended, he was made Administrator of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon his mother's death. When mourning ended, he was appointed Administrator of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召對邇英閣，帝問《乾卦》，昌朝上奏曰：“《乾》之上九稱：‘亢龍有悔。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience in the Zhying Pavilion, the Emperor asked about the Qian hexagram. Changchao submitted: "The top line of Qian reads: 'The dragon flies too high—there is regret.'
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the Zhying Pavilion, the emperor asked about the Qian hexagram. Changchao replied: "The top line of Qian says: 'The dragon flies too high—there is regret.'

sentences.zh: ’悔者，凶災之萌，爻在亢極，必有凶災。

translations.literal: 'Regret' is the sprouting of calamity and disaster. When the line stands at the height of excess, calamity and disaster are sure to follow.
translations.idiomatic: "Regret is the seed of calamity. When a line reaches the extreme of excess, disaster is sure to follow."

sentences.zh: 不言凶而言悔者，以悔有可凶可吉之義，修德則免悔而獲吉矣。

translations.literal: It does not speak of calamity but of regret because regret carries the meaning of possibly turning to calamity or to good fortune. Cultivate virtue and one may escape regret and obtain good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: It speaks of regret rather than calamity because regret can lead either way. Cultivate virtue, and one may escape regret and win good fortune instead.

sentences.zh: ‘用九，見群龍無首，吉’。

translations.literal: 'Employ the nines: behold a host of dragons without a head—good fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: "'Employ the nines: behold a host of dragons without a head—good fortune.'"

sentences.zh: 聖人用剛健之德，乃可決萬機。

translations.literal: The sage ruler employs the virtue of strength and vigor, and only then can he decide the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: A sage ruler must wield the virtue of strength and vigor before he can decide the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 天下久盛，柔不可以濟，然亢而過剛又不能久。

translations.literal: The realm has long flourished; softness alone cannot avail, yet excess and over-rigid strength likewise cannot endure.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has long prospered: softness alone will not suffice, yet excess and overbearing rigidity cannot endure either.

sentences.zh: 獨聖人外以剛健決事，內以謙恭應物，不敢自矜為天下首，乃吉也。”

translations.literal: Only the sage outwardly uses strength and vigor to decide affairs, inwardly meets all things with humility and deference, and dares not set himself up as head of the realm—then there is good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Only the sage decides affairs outwardly with strength and vigor, yet inwardly meets the world with humility and deference, never presuming to be first under Heaven—then there is good fortune.

sentences.zh: 手詔優答。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied with a gracious handwritten edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a gracious handwritten edict.

sentences.zh: 又言：“漢、唐都雍，置三輔內翼京師，朝廷都汴，而近京諸郡皆屬他道，制度不稱王畿。

translations.literal: He also said: "Han and Tang made their capitals at Yong and established the Three Supports to gird the capital from within. Our court is seated at Bian, yet the prefectures near the capital all belong to other circuits—the system does not befit an imperial domain.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Han and Tang made their capitals at Yong and established the Three Supports to shield the capital from within. Our court sits at Bian, yet the prefectures nearest the capital all belong to other circuits—a system unworthy of an imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 請析京東之曹州，京西之陳、許、滑、鄭，皆隸開封府，以四十二縣為京畿。”

translations.literal: I ask that Caozhou of the Eastern Capital circuit and Chen, Xu, Hua, and Zheng of the Western Capital circuit be detached and placed under Kaifeng Prefecture, making forty-two counties the imperial domain.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Caozhou from the Eastern Capital circuit and Chen, Xu, Hua, and Zheng from the Western Capital circuit be detached and placed under Kaifeng Prefecture, making forty-two counties the imperial domain."

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 將行，命講讀官餞於資善堂。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he ordered the lecture and study officials to hold a farewell banquet for him at the Hall of Nurturing Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure, he had the lecture and study officials hold a farewell banquet for him in the Hall of Nurturing Virtue.

sentences.zh: 復判大名府兼河北安撫使。

translations.literal: He was again made Administrator of Daming Prefecture concurrently Hebei Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Administrator of Daming Prefecture and Hebei Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時河決商胡，昌朝請復故道，不從。

translations.literal: At the time the Yellow River broke through at Shanghu. Changchao requested restoring the old channel; [his request] was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Yellow River burst through at Shanghu. Changchao asked that the old channel be restored, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 語在《河渠志》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Treatise on Rivers and Canal Works.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Treatise on Rivers and Canal Works.

sentences.zh: 六塔功敗，濱、棣、德、博民多水死，昌朝振救之甚力。

translations.literal: When the Six Pagodas project failed, many people in Bin, Di, De, and Bo drowned. Changchao worked with great energy to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Pagodas project failed, countless people in Bin, Di, De, and Bo drowned in the floods. Changchao threw himself into relief work with great energy.

sentences.zh: 內侍劉恢往視，還，言河決趙征村，與帝名嫌為不祥，時皆謂昌朝使之以搖當國者。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Liu Hui went to inspect the site. On his return he reported that the river had breached at Zhaozheng Village—a name that clashed with the Emperor's and was taken as inauspicious. At the time all believed Changchao had sent him to unsettle those who held power.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Liu Hui went to inspect the breach. On his return he reported that the river had broken through at Zhaozheng Village—a name too close to the emperor's and therefore taken as ill-omened. At the time many believed Changchao had sent him to shake those then in power.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年，進封許國公，又兼侍中，尋以同中書門下平章事為樞密使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiayou he was advanced to Duke of Xu, also made Palace Attendant. Soon he was changed from Co-Grand Councillor to Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiayou he was promoted to Duke of Xu and also made Palace Attendant. Soon he was shifted from Grand Councillor to Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，宰相文彥博請罷，諫官、御史恐昌朝代彥博，乃相與言昌朝建大第，別創客位以待宦官，宦官有矯制者，樞密院釋不治。

translations.literal: In the third year, Chief Minister Wen Yanbo requested dismissal.
