Remonstrance officials and censors, fearing Changchao would replace Yanbo, together said Changchao had built a great mansion and separately constructed guest quarters to await eunuchs; that when eunuchs had forged edicts, the Bureau of Military Affairs released them without investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year chief minister Wen Yanbo asked to retire. Remonstrance officials and censors, fearing Changchao would succeed him, joined in charging that Changchao had built a grand mansion with separate guest quarters reserved for eunuchs, and that when eunuchs forged edicts the Bureau of Military Affairs let them go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 遂以鎮安軍節度使、右僕射、檢校太師、侍中兼充景靈宮使，出判許州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made Military Commissioner of Zhen'an Army, Right Vice Director, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant concurrently Commissioner of the Jingling Palace, and sent out to administer Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Military Commissioner of Zhen'an, Right Vice Director, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant and Commissioner of the Jingling Palace, and sent out to administer Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以保平軍節度、陝州大都督府長史移大名府兼安撫使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred as Military Commissioner of Baoping Army and Chief Administrator of Shaanzhou Superior Prefecture to Daming Prefecture concurrently Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred from Military Commissioner of Baoping and Chief Administrator of Shaanzhou to Daming Prefecture as Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，徙鳳翔節度使，加左僕射、鳳翔尹，進封魏國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, [Changchao] was transferred to Military Commissioner of Fengxiang, given the additional titles of Left Vice Director and Prefect of Fengxiang, and advanced to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, Changchao was transferred to Military Commissioner of Fengxiang, given the additional titles of Left Vice Director and Prefect of Fengxiang, and promoted to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 治平元年，以侍中守許州，力辭弗許。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiping he was appointed Palace Attendant and guardian of Xuzhou; he pleaded repeatedly but was not permitted to decline.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiping he was appointed Palace Attendant and guardian of Xuzhou. He pleaded hard to be excused, but the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 明年，以疾留京師，乃以左僕射、觀文殿大學士判尚書都省，卒，年六十八，諡曰文元。

translations.literal: The next year, ill, he remained in the capital and was made Left Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, and Administrator of the Secretariat Directorate. He died at sixty-eight; his posthumous title was Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, ill, he stayed in the capital and was made Left Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, and Administrator of the Secretariat Directorate. He died at sixty-eight; his posthumous title was Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 御書墓碑曰“大儒元老之碑”。

translations.literal: The Emperor inscribed his tomb stele: "Stele of the Great Confucian Elder."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally inscribed his tomb stele: "Stele of the Great Confucian Elder."

sentences.zh: 所著《群經音辨》、《通紀》、《時令》、《奏議》、《文集》百二十二卷。

translations.literal: His works included Grouped Classics Phonological Distinctions, Comprehensive Annals, Seasonal Ordinances, Memorials, and Collected Writings—a hundred and twenty-two volumes in all.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Grouped Classics Phonological Distinctions, Comprehensive Annals, Seasonal Ordinances, Memorials, and Collected Writings—one hundred and twenty-two volumes in all.

sentences.zh: 昌朝在侍從，多得名譽。

translations.literal: Changchao, among the attendant officials, won much reputation.
translations.idiomatic: As a court attendant, Changchao won wide esteem.

sentences.zh: 及執政，乃不為正人所與，而數有攻其結宦官、宮人者。

translations.literal: Once in power, upright men would not stand with him, and he was repeatedly attacked for his ties to eunuchs and palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held power, upright men would not stand with him, and he was repeatedly attacked for his ties to eunuchs and palace women.

sentences.zh: 初，昌朝侍講時，同王宗道編修資善堂書籍，其實教授內侍，諫官吳育奏罷之。

translations.literal: Early on, when Changchao served as lecturer-in-waiting, he and Wang Zongdao compiled and edited the Hall of Nurturing Virtue library—but in fact they were instructing inner attendants. Remonstrance official Wu Yu memorialized to have this stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Changchao served as lecturer-in-waiting, he and Wang Zongdao were assigned to compile the Hall of Nurturing Virtue library—but in fact they were teaching inner attendants. Remonstrance official Wu Yu memorialized to have the arrangement abolished.

sentences.zh: 及張方平留唐詢，而詢譖育，世以為昌朝指也。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhang Fangping kept Tang Xun in office and Xun slandered Wu Yu, the world believed Changchao had directed it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Fangping kept Tang Xun in office and Xun slandered Wu Yu, many believed Changchao had put him up to it.

sentences.zh: 然言者謂昌朝釋宦官矯制，後驗問無事實云。

translations.literal: Yet those who spoke of Changchao releasing eunuchs who had forged edicts—when later investigated, there proved to be no truth in it.
translations.idiomatic: As for the charge that Changchao had released eunuchs who forged edicts, later investigation found no truth in it.

sentences.zh: 子章，館閣校勘，蚤世。

translations.literal: His son Zhang was a collator in the Hall of Literature; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang served as collator in the Hall of Literature and died young.

sentences.zh: 青，朝請大夫。

translations.literal: Qing was a Grandee for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Qing rose to Grandee for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 弟昌衡。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Changheng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Changheng.

translations.literal: 〈Younger Brother〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Younger Brother〉

sentences.zh: 昌衡

translations.literal: Changheng
translations.idiomatic: Changheng

sentences.zh: 昌衡字子平。

translations.literal: Changheng, styled Ziping.
translations.idiomatic: Changheng, courtesy name Ziping.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為梓州路轉運判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became transport vice-commissioner of the Zizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and became transport vice-commissioner of the Zizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 賈人請富順井鹽，吏視賄多寡為先後，昌衡一隨月日給之。

translations.literal: Merchants requesting salt from the Fushun wells found that officials prioritized them according to the size of bribes. Changheng simply issued allotments by date of application.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants applying for salt from the Fushun wells found officials ranking requests by the size of the bribe. Changheng simply issued allotments in the order of the calendar.

sentences.zh: 瀘州邊夷蠻，故時守以武吏，昌衡請由東銓調選。

translations.literal: Luzhou bordered the barbarian Yi on the frontier; formerly its prefect was always a military official. Changheng requested that appointments be made through the eastern personnel board instead.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou lay on the frontier among the Yi barbarians, and its prefect had always been a military man. Changheng asked that appointments be made through the eastern personnel board instead.

sentences.zh: 蠻驅馬來市，官第其良駑為二等，上者送秦州，下者輒輕估直而抑買，昌衡請嚴禁之。

translations.literal: The barbarians drove horses to market. Officials graded them as good or poor in two classes: the better ones were sent to Qinzhou; the poorer ones were undervalued and forcibly purchased. Changheng requested that this be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians drove horses to market, officials graded them good or poor in two classes: the better ones were sent on to Qinzhou, while the poorer ones were undervalued and forcibly bought up. Changheng asked that the practice be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 徙提點淮南刑獄、廣東轉運使，徙兩浙路。

translations.literal: He was transferred to intendant of Huainan judicial penalties, Guangdong transport commissioner, and then to the Two Zhe circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to intendant of Huainan judicial penalties, then Guangdong transport commissioner, and then to the Two Zhe circuit.

sentences.zh: 熙寧更法度，核吏治，昌衡數以利害聞，神宗獎其論奏忠益。

translations.literal: During the Xining reforms of law and institutions and the audit of official governance, Changheng repeatedly reported on advantages and disadvantages. Emperor Shenzong commended his memorials as loyal and beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining reforms, as the government overhauled law and audited official conduct, Changheng repeatedly reported on what would help and what would harm. Emperor Shenzong praised his memorials as loyal and useful.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部副使、提舉市易司，課羨，增秩右諫議大夫，加集賢殿修撰、知河南府，曆陳、鄆、應天府、鄧州。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Households Ministry and supervisor of the State Trade Bureau. For surplus revenue he was promoted to Right Remonstrator, given the additional title of Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and made prefect of Henan; he successively governed Chen, Yun, Yingtian, and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice commissioner of the Households Ministry and supervisor of the State Trade Bureau. For meeting surplus revenue targets he was promoted to Right Remonstrator, made compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and appointed prefect of Henan; he went on to govern Chen, Yun, Yingtian, and Deng in succession.

sentences.zh: 以正議大夫致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired as Grandee of Righteous Discussion and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Grandee of Righteous Discussion and died.

sentences.zh: 從子炎。

translations.literal: His nephew was Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew was Yan.

sentences.zh: 〈從子〉

translations.literal: 〈Nephew〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Nephew〉

sentences.zh: 炎

translations.literal: Yan
translations.idiomatic: Yan

sentences.zh: 炎字長卿，以昌朝蔭，更曆筦庫，積遷至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Changqing, entered office through Changchao's yin privilege, served in succession in treasury posts, and rose in cumulative promotion to Vice Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, courtesy name Changqing, entered office through Changchao's yin privilege, served in succession in treasury posts, and rose step by step to Vice Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 政和中，以顯謨閣待制知應天府，徙鄆州、永興。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era he was made Awaiting Draftsman at the Hall of Illustrious Plans and prefect of Yingtian; he was transferred to Yun and Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe era he was made awaiting draftsman at the Hall of Illustrious Plans and prefect of Yingtian, then transferred to Yun and Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 初，陝西行鐵錢久，幣益輕。

translations.literal: Originally iron cash had circulated in Shaanxi for a long time, and the currency grew steadily lighter.
translations.idiomatic: For a long time iron cash had circulated in Shaanxi, and the currency steadily lost weight.

sentences.zh: 蔡京設法盡斂之，更鑄夾錫錢，幣稍重。

translations.literal: Cai Jing devised a method to collect it all in and recoin it as tin-alloy cash, and the currency became somewhat heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing devised a scheme to collect it all and recoin it as tin-alloy cash, and the currency grew somewhat heavier.

sentences.zh: 京去相，轉運使李譓、陳敦復見所斂已多，遽請罷鑄。

translations.literal: When Jing left the chancellorship, transport commissioners Li Xinhui and Chen Dunfu, seeing how much had already been collected, abruptly requested stopping the recoinage.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing left the chancellorship, transport commissioners Li Xinhui and Chen Dunfu, seeing how much had already been collected, abruptly asked that the recoinage be halted.

sentences.zh: 鐵錢既復行，其輕加初，自關以西皆罷市，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Iron cash having been restored to circulation, it was as light as before. From the Pass westward markets shut down everywhere and the people could scarcely live.
translations.idiomatic: Once iron cash circulated again, it was as light as ever. From the Pass westward markets closed everywhere, and the people could scarcely survive.

sentences.zh: 炎獨一切弛禁，聽從其便。

translations.literal: Yan alone lifted all restrictions and let people conduct trade as they saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: Yan alone lifted every restriction and let people trade as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 其後，宣徽使童貫又以兩者重輕相形，遂盡廢夾錫不得用，民益以為苦。

translations.literal: Later, Palace Domestic Service Commissioner Tong Guan, comparing the relative weight of the two kinds of cash, had tin-alloy coins abolished entirely so they could not be used, and the people suffered all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Palace Domestic Service Commissioner Tong Guan, comparing the relative weight of the two currencies, abolished tin-alloy cash altogether so it could no longer be used, and the people suffered all the more.

sentences.zh: 炎徙知延安，因表言：“錢法屢變，人心愈惑。

translations.literal: Yan was transferred to govern Yan'an and submitted a memorial: "The currency law has changed again and again, and popular sentiment grows ever more confused.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was transferred to govern Yan'an and submitted a memorial: "The currency law has changed again and again, and the people grow ever more bewildered.

sentences.zh: 今人以為利者，臣見其害；

translations.literal: What people now take for gain, I see as harm;
translations.idiomatic: What people now call gain, I see as harm;

sentences.zh: 以為是者，臣見其非。

translations.literal: what they take for right, I see as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: what they call right, I see as wrong.

sentences.zh: 中產之家，不過畜夾錫錢一二萬，既棄不用，則惟有守錢而死耳。

translations.literal: A middle-income household holds at most ten or twenty thousand in tin-alloy cash. Now that it is cast aside and useless, they can only sit guarding their coins until they die.
translations.idiomatic: A middle-income household holds at most ten or twenty thousand in tin-alloy cash. Now that it has been cast aside and rendered useless, they can only sit on their coins until they die.

sentences.zh: 邊氓生理蕭條，官又一再變法，鄜延去敵迫近，民殊不安。

translations.literal: Frontier people's livelihoods are withered; the government keeps changing the law again and again. The Yan and Yan circuits lie close to the enemy, and the people are deeply unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier livelihoods are withered, and the government keeps changing the law again and again. The Yan and Yan circuits lie close to the enemy, and the people are deeply unsettled.

sentences.zh: 民不安則邊不可守，願得內郡以養母。”

translations.literal: If the people are unsettled the frontier cannot be held. I wish to be granted an inner circuit post so I may support my mother.
translations.idiomatic: If the people are unsettled, the frontier cannot be held. I ask to be granted an inner prefecture so I may support my mother."

sentences.zh: 乃命為潁州，未行，復留。

translations.literal: He was appointed to Yingzhou but before he could leave was kept at court again.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to Yingzhou, but before he could leave he was kept at court again.

sentences.zh: 又與貫製疆事不合，貫沮之，改河陽，又改鄧州。

translations.literal: He also clashed with Guan over border affairs; Guan obstructed him and he was reassigned to Heyang, then to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He also clashed with Guan over border policy. Guan blocked him, and he was reassigned to Heyang, then to Deng.

sentences.zh: 加直學士、知永興。

translations.literal: He was given the rank of Direct Academician and made prefect of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct Academician and prefect of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 入對，留為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: After an audience he was kept at court as Vice Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience at court he was kept in the capital as Vice Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 貫簽書樞密院河西、北兩房，侍從邀炎俱往賀，炎曰：“故事無簽書兩房者，彼非執政，何賀為？”

translations.literal: When Guan held the concurrent posts of Secretariat signatory for the western and northern chambers of the Bureau of Military Affairs, attendant officials invited Yan to join them in congratulating him. Yan said: "By precedent there is no signatory for two chambers. He is not a chief minister—why congratulate him?"
translations.idiomatic: When Guan was made concurrent signatory for the western and northern chambers of the Bureau of Military Affairs, attendant officials invited Yan to join them in congratulating him. Yan said: "By precedent there is no signatory for two chambers at once. He is not a chief minister—why congratulate him?"

sentences.zh: 會以疾卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: At this juncture he died of illness at fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Just then he died of illness at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Grandee of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grandee of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 〈伯祖父〉

translations.literal: 〈Father's Elder Uncle〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Father's Elder Uncle〉

sentences.zh: 琰

translations.literal: Yan
translations.idiomatic: Yan

sentences.zh: 琰風神峻整，有吏幹，佐太宗居幕府凡五年，勤於所職。

translations.literal: Yan had a severe, composed bearing and administrative talent. He assisted Taizong in his headquarters for five years in all, diligent in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had a stern, composed bearing and real administrative talent. He served Taizong in his headquarters for five years in all, diligent in every duty.

sentences.zh: 昆弟五人，琰最幼，及琰曆官而諸兄相繼死。

translations.literal: There were five brothers; Yan was the youngest. By the time Yan had risen through office, his elder brothers had died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: There were five brothers, and Yan was the youngest. By the time Yan had risen through office, his elder brothers had died one after another.

sentences.zh: 琰拊循孤幼，聚族凡百口，分給衣食，庭無間言，士大夫以此稱之。

translations.literal: Yan nurtured the orphaned young, gathered the clan—nearly a hundred mouths—and apportioned food and clothing. There was no discord in the household, and scholar-officials praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yan nurtured the orphaned young, gathered the clan—nearly a hundred mouths—and apportioned food and clothing among them. There was no discord in the household, and scholar-officials praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 琰子湜、汾。

translations.literal: Yan's sons were Shi and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's sons were Shi and Fen.

sentences.zh: 湜至軍器庫使。

translations.literal: Shi rose to Commissioner of the Arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: Shi rose to Commissioner of the Arsenal.

sentences.zh: 交阯黎桓之篡丁璿也，朝廷以孫全興將兵討焉。

translations.literal: When Li Huan of Jiaozhi usurped Ding Sui, the court sent Sun Quanxing at the head of an army to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huan of Jiaozhi usurped Ding Sui, the court sent Sun Quanxing at the head of an army to punish him.

sentences.zh: 湜與王僎同掌軍事，黎桓偽降，全興信之，軍遂北，湜、僎並坐失律誅。

translations.literal: Shi and Wang Zhen jointly directed military affairs. Li Huan feigned surrender; Quanxing believed him, and the army turned north. Shi and Zhen were both executed for breach of military discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Wang Zhen jointly directed military affairs. Li Huan feigned surrender, Quanxing believed him, and the army withdrew north. Shi and Zhen were both executed for breach of military discipline.

sentences.zh: 汾至殿中丞。

translations.literal: Fen rose to Palace Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Fen rose to Palace Aide.

sentences.zh: 湜子昌符，賜同學究出身。

translations.literal: Shi's son Changfu was granted the status of a fellow licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's son Changfu was granted the status of a fellow licentiate.

sentences.zh: 汾子昌齡，第進士，為屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: Fen's son Changling passed the jinshi examination and served as Outer Director of the Bureau of State Farms.
translations.idiomatic: Fen's son Changling passed the jinshi examination and served as outer director of the Bureau of State Farms.

sentences.zh: 梁適，字仲賢，東平人，翰林學士顥之子也。

translations.literal: Liang Shi, styled Zhongxian, was a native of Dongping and son of Hanlin Academician Liang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shi, courtesy name Zhongxian, was a native of Dongping and the son of Hanlin Academician Liang Hao.

sentences.zh: 少孤，嘗輯父遺文及所自著以進，真宗曰：“梁顥有子矣。”

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he once compiled his father's posthumous writings together with his own compositions and presented them. Zhenzong said: "Liang Hao has left a son."
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he once compiled his father's posthumous writings together with his own work and presented them to the throne. Zhenzong said: "Liang Hao has left a son."

sentences.zh: 授秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He was granted the post of Collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the post of collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為開封工曹，知昆山縣。

translations.literal: He served as Works Officer of Kaifeng and prefect of Kunshan County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as works officer of Kaifeng and prefect of Kunshan County.

sentences.zh: 徙梧州，奏罷南漢時民間折稅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wuzhou and memorialized to abolish the fold-tax levied on the people during the Southern Han period.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wuzhou and memorialized to abolish the fold-tax the people had borne since the Southern Han.

sentences.zh: 更舉進士，知淮陽軍，又奏減京東預買紬百三十萬。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination by special recommendation, served as prefect of Huaiyang Army, and again memorialized to reduce eastern Jingdong's pre-purchase silk by 1.3 million.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi by special recommendation, became prefect of Huaiyang Army, and again memorialized to cut eastern Jingdong's pre-purchase silk quota by 1.3 million.

sentences.zh: 論景祐赦書不當錄朱梁後，仁宗記其名，尋召為審刑詳議官。

translations.literal: He argued that the Jingyou amnesty proclamation should not list descendants of the Later Liang; Renzong noted his name and soon summoned him as detailed deliberation officer of the Office of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the Jingyou amnesty should not list descendants of the Later Liang. Renzong noted his name and soon made him detailed deliberation officer of the Office of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 梓州妖人白彥歡依鬼神以詛殺人，獄具，以無傷讞。

translations.literal: In Zizhou, the sorcerer Bai Yanhuan relied on spirits to curse people to death; when the case was complete, he was sentenced on the ground of no physical injury.
translations.idiomatic: In Zizhou, the sorcerer Bai Yanhuan used spirits to curse people to death. When the case was complete, the court sentenced him on the ground that no physical injury had occurred.

sentences.zh: 適駁曰：“殺人以刃或可拒，而詛可拒乎？

translations.literal: Shi rebutted: "Killing with a blade can perhaps be resisted, but can a curse be resisted?
translations.idiomatic: Shi rebutted: "One might resist a blade, but how does one resist a curse?

sentences.zh: 是甚於刃也。”

translations.literal: This is worse than a blade."
translations.idiomatic: That is worse than a blade."

sentences.zh: 卒論死。

translations.literal: In the end he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Bai was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 有鳥似鶴集端門，稍下及庭中，大臣或倡以為瑞，適曰“此野鳥入宮庭耳，何瑞之云？”

translations.literal: A bird resembling a crane gathered at the Duan Gate, gradually descending into the courtyard; some ministers proposed it as an auspicious sign. Shi said, "This is merely a wild bird entering the palace courtyard—what auspiciousness is there to speak of?
translations.idiomatic: A crane-like bird gathered at the Duan Gate and gradually descended into the courtyard. Some ministers proposed it as an auspicious omen. Shi said, "This is only a wild bird in the palace courtyard—what omen is there in that?

sentences.zh: 嘗與同院燕肅奏何次公案，帝顧曰：“次公似是漢時人字。”

translations.literal: Once, together with his colleague in the same office Yan Su, he reported on the case of He Cigong. The emperor looked up and said: "Cigong seems to be the style of a Han dynasty man."
translations.idiomatic: Once, together with his colleague Yan Su, he reported on the case of He Cigong. The emperor looked up and said, "Cigong seems to be the style of a Han man."

sentences.zh: 肅不能對，適進曰：“蓋寬饒、黃霸皆字次公。”

translations.literal: Su could not reply; Shi stepped forward and said: "Both Gai Kuangrao and Huang Ba were styled Cigong."
translations.idiomatic: Su could not answer. Shi stepped forward and said, "Both Gai Kuangrao and Huang Ba were styled Cigong."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，因詢適家世，益器之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and inquired into Shi's family background, esteeming him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, inquired into Shi's family background, and esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 他日宰相擬適提點刑獄，帝曰：“姑留之，俟諫官有闕，可用也。”

translations.literal: Another day the chief ministers proposed appointing Shi as judicial intendant; the emperor said: "For now keep him here—when a remonstrator's post falls vacant, he may be used."
translations.idiomatic: Another day the chief ministers proposed appointing Shi judicial intendant. The emperor said, "Keep him here for now. When a remonstrator's post opens, he can be used."

sentences.zh: 遂拜右正言。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 林瑀由中旨侍講天章閣，適疏其過。

translations.literal: Lin Yu, by an order from the inner court, was lecturing at the Hall of Heaven's Manifestations; Shi memorialized against his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yu, by imperial order from the inner court, was lecturing at the Hall of Heaven's Manifestations. Shi memorialized against his faults.

sentences.zh: 又言：“夏守贇為將無功，不宜復典宥密。”

translations.literal: He also said: "Xia Shouyun as a general achieved nothing and should not again be put in charge of Youmi."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Xia Shouyun achieved nothing as a general and should not again head military affairs."

sentences.zh: 會婦黨任中師執政，以嫌改直史館，修起居注。

translations.literal: As it happened, his wife's relative Ren Zhongshi held power; on account of the conflict of interest he was changed to Compiler in the Historiography Office and recorder of the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, his wife's kinsman Ren Zhongshi was in power; on account of the conflict of interest he was moved to compiler in the Historiography Office and recorder of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 奉使陝西，與范仲淹條邊機十餘事。

translations.literal: On a mission to Shaanxi, he set forth with Fan Zhongyan more than ten matters concerning border strategy.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Shaanxi, he and Fan Zhongyan laid out more than ten matters of border strategy.

sentences.zh: 進知制誥、權發遣開封府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to drafter of proclamations and acting commissioner of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of proclamations and acting commissioner of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出知兗州。

translations.literal: After little more than a year, he was sent out as prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year, he was sent out as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 萊蕪冶鐵為民病，當役者率破產以償，適募人為之，自是民不憂冶戶，而鐵歲溢。

translations.literal: Iron smelting at Laiwu was a hardship for the people; those liable for corvée labor invariably ruined their estates to meet the obligation. Shi hired laborers to do the work; from then on the people no longer feared the iron foundries, and iron production overflowed year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Iron smelting at Laiwu was a scourge on the people; those liable for corvée duty often ruined their households paying the levy. Shi hired laborers to do the work instead, and from then on the people no longer feared the iron foundries while iron output overflowed year by year.

sentences.zh: 再遷樞密直學士、知延州。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to academician directly attached to military affairs and prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 告歸治葬，過京師，得入見，自言前為朋黨擠逐，留為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return home and arrange a funeral; passing through the capital, he gained an audience, said he had earlier been driven out by factional rivals, and was retained as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave to go home and arrange a funeral. Passing through the capital, he gained an audience, said he had earlier been driven out by factional rivals, and was kept on as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 御史交劾之，以侍讀學士知澶州，徙秦州。

translations.literal: Censors jointly impeached him; he was made Academic Reader and prefect of Cizhou, then transferred to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censors jointly impeached him. He was made academic reader and prefect of Cizhou, then transferred to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 入知審刑院，擢樞密副使。

translations.literal: Called in to direct the Office of Judicial Review, he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to direct the Office of Judicial Review, he was promoted to vice commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 張堯佐一日除四使，言者爭之力，帝頗怒。

translations.literal: Zhang Yaozuo was in one day appointed to four commissioner posts; remonstrators argued against it with all their strength, and the emperor was quite angry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yaozuo was in one day given four commissioner appointments. Remonstrators argued against it with all their strength, and the emperor grew quite angry.

sentences.zh: 適曰：“台諫論事，職耳。

translations.literal: Shi said: "For the Censorate and remonstrators to criticize affairs is their duty, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "For censors and remonstrators to criticize affairs is simply their duty.

sentences.zh: 堯佐恩實過，恐非所以全之。”

translations.literal: Yaozuo's favor has truly gone too far—this may not be the way to protect him."
translations.idiomatic: Yaozuo's favor has truly gone too far. This may not be the way to protect him."

sentences.zh: 遂奪二使。

translations.literal: Two of the appointments were then revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Two of the appointments were then revoked.

sentences.zh: 儂智高入寇，移嫚書求邕、桂節度，帝將受其降。

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao invaded, sent an insolent letter demanding the military governorships of Yong and Gui, and the emperor was about to accept his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Nong Zhigao invaded, sent an insolent letter demanding the military governorships of Yong and Gui, and the emperor was about to accept his surrender.

sentences.zh: 適曰：“若爾，嶺外非朝廷有矣。”

translations.literal: Shi said: "If so, the lands beyond the mountains will no longer belong to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "If that were done, the lands beyond the mountains would no longer belong to the court."

sentences.zh: 乃遣狄青討之。

translations.literal: Di Qing was then dispatched to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing was then dispatched to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 賊平，帝曰：“向非適言，南方安危，未可知也。”

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the emperor said: "Had it not been for Shi's words, the safety of the south would have been unknowable."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, the emperor said, "Had Shi not spoken as he did, the south's safety would have been unknowable."

sentences.zh: 遷參知政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 契丹欲易國書稱南北朝，適曰：“宋之為宋，受之於天，不可改也。

translations.literal: The Khitan wished to change the national letters to call themselves Northern and Southern Dynasties. Shi said: "Song is Song, received from Heaven—it cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan wished to change the state letters so both sides would be called Northern and Southern Dynasties. Shi said, "Song is Song, received from Heaven—it cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 契丹亦其國名，自古豈有無名之國哉？”

translations.literal: Khitan is also their state's name—since antiquity, has there ever been a nameless state?"
translations.idiomatic: Khitan is also their state's name. Since antiquity, has there ever been a nameless state?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 進同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Councilor of the Tongzhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi rank and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to grand councilor and grand academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

sentences.zh: 大璫王守忠求為節度使，適持不可；

translations.literal: The great eunuch Wang Shouzhong sought appointment as military commissioner; Shi maintained this was impermissible;
translations.idiomatic: The great eunuch Wang Shouzhong sought appointment as military commissioner; Shi maintained this was impermissible;

sentences.zh: 張貴妃治喪皇儀殿，又以為不可。

translations.literal: Concubine Zhang's funeral rites in the Hall of Imperial Rites—again he deemed it impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: When Concubine Zhang's funeral was to be held in the Hall of Imperial Rites, again he deemed it impermissible.

sentences.zh: 將以適為園陵使，適言國朝以來無此制，由是浸與陳執中不合。

translations.literal: The court was about to appoint Shi imperial tomb commissioner; Shi said there had been no such regulation since the founding of the dynasty, and from this gradually fell out with Chen Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was about to appoint Shi imperial tomb commissioner, Shi said there had been no such practice since the dynasty's founding, and from this he gradually fell out with Chen Zhizhong.

sentences.zh: 適曉暢法令，臨事有膽力，而多挾智數，不為清議所許。

translations.literal: Shi was thoroughly versed in statutes, bold and resolute in action, yet often relied on stratagems and was not approved by pure critics.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was thoroughly versed in law, bold and resolute in action, yet often relied on stratagems and won no approval from the moral critics.

sentences.zh: 御史馬遵、吳中復極論其貪黷怙權，罷知鄭州。

translations.literal: Censors Ma Zun and Wu Zhongfu argued forcefully that he was corrupt and abused power; he was dismissed to prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Ma Zun and Wu Zhongfu argued forcefully that he was corrupt and abused power. He was dismissed to prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 京師茶賈負公錢四十萬緡，鹽鐵判官李虞卿案之急，賈懼，與吏為市，內交於適子弟，適出虞卿提點陝西刑獄。

translations.literal: A Kaifeng tea merchant owed four hundred thousand strings of public money; Li Yuqing, vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Bureau, pressed the case urgently. The merchant, in fear, made a deal with clerks and secretly contacted Shi's sons and younger brothers; Shi had Yuqing transferred out as judicial intendant of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: A Kaifeng tea merchant owed the government four hundred thousand strings. Li Yuqing, vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Bureau, pressed the case hard. The merchant, in fear, struck a deal with clerks and secretly reached Shi's sons and younger brothers. Shi had Yuqing transferred out as judicial intendant of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 及罷，帝即還虞卿三司。

translations.literal: When Shi was dismissed, the emperor immediately restored Yuqing to the Three Departments Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi was dismissed, the emperor immediately restored Yuqing to the Three Departments Commission.

sentences.zh: 復加觀文殿大學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: He was again made Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 古渭初建砦，間為屬羌所鈔，益兵拒守，羌復驚疑。

translations.literal: At Guwei a fort was newly built; intermittently it was raided by dependent Qiang tribes, and when troops were added to hold it, the Qiang again grew alarmed and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: At Guwei a fort was newly built. It was intermittently raided by dependent Qiang tribes, and when more troops were added to hold it, the Qiang grew alarmed and suspicious again.

sentences.zh: 適具牛酒，召諭其種人，且罷所益兵，羌不為患。

translations.literal: Shi prepared cattle and wine, summoned and admonished the tribal leaders, and moreover withdrew the added troops; the Qiang caused no further trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Shi prepared cattle and wine, summoned the tribal leaders to counsel them, and withdrew the added troops. The Qiang caused no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 徙永興軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 夏人盜耕屈野河西田累年，朝廷欲正封，以適為定國軍節度使、知并州，至則悉復侵地六百里。

translations.literal: For years the Tangut people had illegally farmed fields west of the Quye River; the court wished to rectify the borders and appointed Shi military commissioner of Dingguo Army and prefect of Bingzhou; on arrival he fully recovered six hundred li of encroached territory.
translations.idiomatic: For years the Tangut had illegally farmed fields west of the Quye River. The court wished to rectify the borders and appointed Shi military commissioner of Dingguo Army and prefect of Bingzhou. On arrival he recovered the full six hundred li of encroached land.

sentences.zh: 還，知河陽，領忠武、昭德二鎮、檢校太師，復為觀文殿大學士，以太子太保致仕，進太傅。

translations.literal: Returning, he served as prefect of Heyang, held the two commands of Zhongwu and Zhaode, was made Honorary Grand Preceptor, again became Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, retired as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and was advanced to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he served as prefect of Heyang, held the two commands of Zhongwu and Zhaode, was made honorary grand preceptor, again became grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, retired as grand guardian of the heir apparent, and was advanced to grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, he died at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining he died at age seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈司空兼侍中，諡曰莊肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Sikong with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant; posthumous title Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded Sikong with concurrent appointment as palace attendant; his posthumous title was Zhuangsu.

translations.literal: 〈Grandson〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Grandson〉

sentences.zh: 子美

translations.literal: Zimei
translations.idiomatic: Zimei

sentences.zh: 孫子美，紹聖中，提舉湖南常平。

translations.literal: Sun Zimei, during the Shaosheng era, served as intendant of the Hunan Ever-Normal Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zimei, during the Shaosheng era, served as intendant of the Hunan Ever-Normal Granary.

sentences.zh: 時新復役法，子美先諸路成役書，就遷提點刑獄。

translations.literal: When the corvée labor law was newly restored, Zimei completed the corvée registers ahead of the other circuits and was promoted on the spot to judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the corvée law was newly restored, Zimei completed the corvée registers ahead of every other circuit and was promoted on the spot to judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國初，除尚書郎中，中書舍人鄒浩封還之，改京西轉運副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong Jingguo, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of the Interior; Central Secretariat Drafter Zou Hao returned the sealed appointment, and he was changed to Vice Transport Commissioner of the Jingxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong Jingguo he was appointed director in the Ministry of the Interior. Central Secretariat drafter Zou Hao returned the sealed appointment, and he was changed to vice transport commissioner of the Jingxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫陳次升又言：“子美緣章惇姻家，連使湖外，承迎其旨意，一時逐臣在封部者，多被其虐，不宜使在近畿。”

translations.literal: Remonstrating Grandee Chen Cisheng also said: "Zimei, through his marriage tie to Zhang Dun, was sent in succession to posts beyond the lakes, carrying out Dun's wishes; many exiled officials within his jurisdiction at the time suffered harsh treatment at his hands—he should not be posted near the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating grandee Chen Cisheng also said, "Zimei, through his marriage tie to Zhang Dun, was sent in succession to posts beyond the lakes, carrying out Dun's wishes. Many exiled officials within his jurisdiction at the time suffered at his hands. He should not be posted near the capital."

sentences.zh: 及徙成都路，累遷直龍圖閣、河北都轉運使，傾漕計以奉上，至捐緡錢三百萬市北珠以進。

translations.literal: When transferred to the Chengdu circuit, he was promoted in succession to Academic Expositor of the Longtu Hall and Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei; he drained transport revenue to serve the throne, going so far as to donate three million strings to purchase northern pearls for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Chengdu circuit and promoted in succession to academic expositor of the Longtu Hall and chief transport commissioner of Hebei. He drained transport revenue to serve the throne, going so far as to donate three million strings to buy northern pearls for presentation.

sentences.zh: 崇寧間，諸路漕臣進羨餘，自子美始。

translations.literal: During the Chongning era, transport commissioners throughout the circuits began presenting surpluses—it began with Zimei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era, transport commissioners throughout the circuits began presenting surpluses—it began with Zimei.

sentences.zh: 北珠出女真，子美市於契丹，契丹嗜其利，虐女真捕海東青以求珠。

translations.literal: Northern pearls came from the Jurchen; Zimei purchased them from the Khitan. The Khitan, greedy for profit, abused the Jurchen to hunt gyrfalcons in exchange for pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Northern pearls came from the Jurchen. Zimei bought them from the Khitan, and the Khitan, greedy for profit, abused the Jurchen, forcing them to hunt gyrfalcons in exchange for pearls.

sentences.zh: 兩國之禍蓋基於此，子美用是致位光顯。

translations.literal: The calamities of both states were rooted in this; by it Zimei rose to dazzling prominence.
translations.idiomatic: The calamities of both states were rooted in this, and by it Zimei rose to dazzling prominence.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，以疾罷為開府儀同三司、提舉嵩山崇福宮，卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, dismissed on account of illness, he was made Grandee of Splendid State with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies and superintendent of the Songshan Chongfu Palace; he died and was posthumously awarded Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuanhe he was dismissed on account of illness, made grandee of splendid state with equipage equal to the three excellencies and superintendent of the Songshan Chongfu Palace. He died and was posthumously awarded junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 子美為郡，縱侈殘虐，然有幹才，所至辦治雲。

translations.literal: As a prefect, Zimei was extravagant and cruel, yet possessed real ability; wherever he was posted he managed affairs with remarkable effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: As a prefect, Zimei was extravagant and cruel, yet possessed real ability. Wherever he was posted, he ran affairs with notable efficiency.

sentences.zh: 論曰：此五人者，皆以文吏為宰相。

translations.literal: Commentary: These five men all rose from civil clerks to chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: These five men all rose from civil clerks to chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 執中建儲一言，適契上意，不然，何超遷之驟也。

translations.literal: Zhizhong's single word on establishing the heir apparent exactly matched the emperor's mind—otherwise, how could Hang's rapid promotions be explained?
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong's single word on establishing the heir apparent happened to match the emperor's mind—otherwise, how explain Hang's sudden, rapid rise?

sentences.zh: 然與劉沆皆寡學少文，希世用事。

translations.literal: Yet he and Liu Hang both had little learning and scant literary polish, currying favor with the age to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he and Liu Hang both had little learning and scant literary polish, currying favor with the times to wield power.

sentences.zh: 馮拯議論多迎合王意，昌朝明經術而尚阿私，梁適曉法令而挾智術，斯君子所不與也。

translations.literal: Feng Zheng's opinions mostly catered to the emperor's wishes; Changchao was versed in classical learning yet inclined to favoritism; Liang Shi knew statutes yet relied on cunning stratagems—these are men a gentleman would not associate with.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zheng's opinions mostly catered to the emperor's wishes; Changchao was versed in classical learning yet inclined to favoritism; Liang Shi knew the law yet relied on cunning stratagems—these are not men a gentleman would keep company with.

sentences.zh: 若執中不受私謁，沆臨事強果，拯從容一言免謂於誅死，此又足稱者焉。

translations.literal: Yet if Zhizhong would accept no private audiences, if Hang was forceful and resolute in action, if Zheng with a single calm word spared Wei from execution—these too are things worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhizhong would accept no private audiences, Hang was forceful and resolute in action, and Zheng with a single calm word spared Wei from execution—these too are things worthy of praise.
